verify:event-detail.current_state_summary: Tapping a billboard, pin or 3D lot on the map sets a selected id in page state (src/app/page.tsx:50, 137; NightMap.tsx:344, 351, 621-625). That mounts EventCard, a dark card up to 64% of the screen tall floating over the map (EventCard.tsx:84). At the same moment the camera dives to zoom 15.6 or closer with a 55-degree tilt (NightMap.tsx:682-698). That puts it inside the extruded 3D city (from zoom 13, mapStyle.ts:107-135) and next to every event's toy-scale house with an orange/ember roof (eventLots.ts:44-56). The orange heat glow is still drawn on top of all of it at about 28% opacity (NightMap.tsx:212-233). The fixed top of the card has a source label, an 18px title, and a dim 11px mono line with venue, area, date and time. Below that are three tiny stat tiles (price in orange, a rough travel estimate, a modelled 'right now' crowd label), then a CHECK IN · +50 XP button that stays greyed out for anyone more than 1.5 km away, plus unlabelled chat and external-link icons (EventCard.tsx:87-124). findings.title: Cut the 'How the night goes · expected' crowd chart
findings.evidence: src/components/EventCard.tsx:169-190 draws an 8-bar chart from nightProfile() (src/lib/crowd.ts:74-81), computed at EventCard.tsx:77-78. Bars are painted orange and Ember (EventCard.tsx:177). The caption explains the model: 'Built from how many Hoppers swiped in and how Lagos nights usually run. Peaks around…' (186-190). The curve is a hard-coded shape (crowd.ts:18-26) multiplied by the heat score (crowd.ts:29). The one real number in the block is event.checkins (189), which is the event's total check-ins (supabase/schema.sql:211, 217) but is labelled 'tonight'.
findings.why: Jae asked for this cut by name. It also breaks the system in three ways. It shows a model's guess as if it were data. It uses orange on a chart nobody can tap ('Orange is a verb… Nothing orange is ever inert'). It uses Ember, which the draft reserves for the button lip. The draft also says working UI should be 'flat, high contrast and deliberately plain'.
findings.suggestion: Delete the whole block. Engineers also remove the lines that only feed it (EventCard.tsx:77-78, and nightProfile in the import at line 14). The real fact, how many Hoppers have checked in, moves into the guest-list row of the new event page (see the stub + guest list finding).
findings.gamification_angle: A count of real Hoppers who are going or already there is more motivating than a modelled curve.

findings.title: Rebuild the top of the event page: big ticket stub, guest list above the fold, and an 'I'M GOING' lip button that stamps your face
findings.evidence: Today's top section (EventCard.tsx:87-124) has an 18px title (92), a dim mono venue/date line (93-95), three tiny stat tiles (97-110) and a primary CHECK IN button (113-115). That button reads 'GET CLOSER TO CHECK IN' and stays disabled outside 1.5 km (CHECKIN_RADIUS_M, src/lib/useCheckin.ts:9), which covers almost everyone planning a night out. For community leads it is a disabled 'VERIFY DETAILS BEFORE CHECK-IN' button (113). The card has no 'going' action at all. Going only exists as a swipe in Discover, which writes to the swipes table (src/app/discover/page.tsx:56-58). The total comes back as swipes_in (src/lib/types.ts:17) and is shown only as a tiny grey tag (EventCard.tsx:133). Swipes are read-own only (supabase/schema.sql:433-434). There are insert and delete policies (436, 438-439) but no update policy. A stamp keyframe already exists (src/app/globals.css:192-201) but is only used, with an elastic overshoot, in the intro (TitleSequence.tsx:367).
findings.why: Design draft §07 screen 04 asks for 'Big stub, lineup, price, ticket link out, guest list above the fold' and says '"I'm going" stamps your face onto the guest list in place, without navigating anywhere.' The ticket stub is the container for anything that represents one night. Right now the main button on the most-opened screen is greyed out for most people.
findings.suggestion: New layout, top to bottom. (1) Ticket stub. The flyer as an art strip if there is one. The title in Poppins Black, about 28-32px. One DM Mono line such as 'FRI 10 OCT · 10PM · LEKKI PHASE 1 · ₦10,000'. The venue name in Archivo. Two punched notches on the sides. At most one coloured state pill. (2) Guest list. The going count as a big 32px Poppins Black number with a mono caption 'HOPPERS GOING', then a row of face slots. (3) One full-width orange lip button, 'I'M GOING'. On tap, your face stamps into the first slot (180ms, hard ease-out, no overshoot; reuse the existing stamp keyframe). The button then becomes a transparent pill with a thin green border reading 'YOU'RE GOING ✓', with a small 'undo' text link. Not a green-filled button: green may never fill a surface. (4) A secondary row: 'TICKETS ↗' (the existing ig_url link, replacing the unlabelled icon at 119-123) and 'SHARE'. When you are within 1.5 km (the same closeEnough test as today, line 72; the server allows check-in at any time), the main slot becomes 'CHECK IN' using the existing onCheckIn. For leads, the main button becomes 'CHECK LISTING ↗' instead of a disabled button. Engineering notes, all client-only: 'I'm going' reuses the swipes write from discover/page.tsx:56-58. Because there is no update policy, switching an earlier 'pass' to 'going' must delete then insert, not upsert. 'Undo' is a delete, which is allowed. 'Am I going' reuses the own-swipes read (discover/page.tsx:29). Bump the count by one in the UI straight away, because swipes_in only refreshes on the 5-minute reload (src/lib/useEvents.ts:66). Your face is profile.avatar (page.tsx:42), drawn with src/components/Avatar.tsx. Other Hoppers' faces cannot be read today, so v1 shows the count, your face, and '+22 others'. The draft's install sheet is meant to fire after the first 'I'm going', so this is also its trigger point.
findings.gamification_angle: This is the event page's one gamified moment, the way the draft defines it: your face stamped onto the list in place. It turns 'going' from a private swipe into a visible, social act.

findings.title: Cut the three stat tiles (price / travel time / 'right now')
findings.evidence: EventCard.tsx:97-110 renders three Stat tiles. 'Price' is orange text (98 passes hot, and 270 turns that into text-orange). 'To get there ~N MIN' comes from travelEstimate, a rough formula of 2.4 min/km + 5 min, + 18 min if you cross a bridge; the code itself calls it 'Rough' (src/lib/geo.ts:57-69). With no location it shows 'SET LOCATION', which looks tappable but sits in a plain div (101, 268). 'Right now' is a modelled crowd label with a diamond coloured from TONE_HEX, which uses orange and Ember as crowd states (src/lib/crowd.ts:44-49). Labels are 8px and values 12px (EventCard.tsx:266-277). The billboard you just tapped already shows price · time · minutes (src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:646-647).
findings.why: The draft says numbers are display type: '32px and up in Poppins Black, tabular, with a mono caption… Never set a stat as body text.' It also says orange is only for things you can tap and Ember only for the lip. Travel time is a guess, and all three facts repeat the billboard.
findings.suggestion: Delete the three tiles and the Stat component. Price moves into the stub's mono line, in cream rather than orange. Drop travel time; if Jae wants distance, add a dim mono 'ABOUT 12 KM' to the stub line. Replace 'Right now' with plain text in the guest-list row, shown only while the event is live: '14 HERE NOW' (here_now is already on the event row, types.ts:19).

findings.title: Remove the quest list from the event page
findings.evidence: EventCard.tsx:136 mounts EventQuestList. EventQuestList.tsx:18 keeps every quest with no event attached (!quest.event_id || quest.event_id === eventId), so every city-wide quest shows on every event. Each quest brings its own controls: a venue-code field and QR button (64-67), a free-text box (68), a crew dropdown (69-74) and its own 'DO THIS · EARN XP' button (75-77). The block sits on an orange-tinted surface (33), uses symbol/emoji icons 📸 ▦ ✦ (52) and orange '+N XP' tags (57). The same quests, with the same inputs and an event picker, already live on /quests (src/app/quests/page.tsx:28-37). findings.why: It is the biggest block on the card and sits directly under the header, pushing the real event information down. Most of it isn't about this event. The draft says 'Each gets one gamified moment; the rest of the screen does its job quietly.' An orange-tinted panel is decorative orange, which the system forbids.
findings.suggestion: Take the quest list off the event page; quests keep living on /quests. Keep the 'add a photo' link on the event page after check-in, because photo quests depend on it. If Jae wants a nudge, show one dim mono line, only after check-in and only for quests tied to this exact event: '2 QUESTS HERE →', linking to /quests. No forms on the event page.
findings.gamification_angle: Quests stay a game on their own page. The event page stays about the night out.

findings.title: Opening an event dives the camera into the 3D city and under the orange heat glow: this is when the 'orange buildings around events' appear
findings.evidence: On select, NightMap.tsx:682-698 eases to zoom 15.6 or closer at a 55-degree tilt; the comment says 'so the venue's lot stands up in 3D'. Three things then colour the area around the venue orange. (a) The illustrated city: from zoom 13 every OpenMapTiles building is extruded, heights are exaggerated 2.2x, and the colour ramps to Ember (src/lib/mapStyle.ts:104-135). It grows with an overshoot animation (riseCity, mapStyle.ts:141-151) the first time the camera passes zoom 13.4 (NightMap.tsx:181-189). The opening swoop stops at 12.2 or 11.2 (NightMap.tsx:791), so the first event tap is usually what triggers it. (b) The heat layer: violet → Ember → orange → cream (NightMap.tsx:222-231). It is added with no layer-order hint, so it draws on top of the buildings and lots (212). At the 15.6 dive it is still at about 0.28 opacity (221) with an ~85px radius (220), which washes orange over every building around the venue. (c) Every event, not just the selected one, gets a 120 m-wide toy house with Ember eaves, an orange ridge and a crowd-coloured diamond (src/lib/eventLots.ts:8-9, 44-56; layer at NightMap.tsx:192-208, data for all events at 402-409). The card then covers up to 64% of the screen anyway (EventCard.tsx:84).
findings.why: Jae wants 3D models only where events are, and the orange buildings that surround events when you zoom in must go. For most users, tapping an event is what triggers that zoom. Orange on non-tappable buildings and on the glow also breaks 'orange is a verb'. The overshoot rise breaks 'stamp, not bounce' and 'everywhere else, nothing moves'.
findings.suggestion: When an event opens, glide to the venue at about zoom 15 with a gentle tilt (about 35°) instead of 55°, so only that event's own model stands up. Engineers: stay at or above zoom 14.6 (STREET_ZOOM, NightMap.tsx:58) so the pin-to-lot handover and the sign lift (485-490) still line up. While the event page is open, hide the heat glow, or at least draw it under the buildings and lots. Remove the city building layer and its rise animation completely (stop calling addCityLayer/riseCity at NightMap.tsx:180-189; the map audit owns this). Keep one small model per event, since that is 'models only where events are'. Unselected models use ground tones (#2E2320 roof, cream walls) and only the selected one turns orange, so it reads as 'the one you tapped'. Lots are tappable (NightMap.tsx:351), so orange there is allowed.
findings.gamification_angle: One glowing model where the night is reads as a destination. A whole orange city reads as noise.

findings.title: Merge the two violet reward boxes into one 'drop' line that hands off to the drop reveal
findings.evidence: Game drops: EventCard.tsx:138-149. This is a violet-filled panel (bg-violet/10, 139) with a 🎁 emoji (142), a QR text field and inline camera scanner (143, 147), an OPEN DROP button (144), and the prize shown as a small inline box with an orange 'YOU GOT' label (146). Every drop on the card shares one QR input (dropCode, 55, used at 143), so with two drops, typing in one fills both. Collectibles: a second violet-filled box (151-167) with emoji items (159; collectibles also have an art_url, src/lib/useCollectibles.ts:6), a COLLECT button per item (161-163) and a COLLECTION → link (155). Drops already carry opens_at (src/lib/game.ts:7). The four-box reveal doesn't exist anywhere yet: /drops also reveals inline as 'YOU GOT' (src/app/drops/page.tsx).
findings.why: The draft says 'Tier 2 never paints a surface' and 'The drop reveal is the only extravagance': four sealed boxes, tear, flick. Revealing the prize as a small text box inside a scrolling card throws that moment away. Two reward systems in two boxes on one card is confusing.
findings.suggestion: Put one violet pill on the stub: 'DROP AT 11PM' (from opens_at) or 'DROP LIVE'. Below the guest list, show one quiet row: a violet dot plus 'A drop is hidden here · open it at the venue'. When you're close enough, it becomes a lip button 'OPEN DROP' that opens the full-screen drop reveal; the QR entry moves into that screen too. Until the reveal screen is built, the button goes to /drops. Collectibles fold into the same row (for example '+1 collectible', using the art image instead of emoji) instead of their own box. Claiming works exactly as now (same claimDrop and collect calls).
findings.gamification_angle: This keeps the drop reveal as the app's one big payoff instead of a text box.

findings.title: Make the event page shareable on WhatsApp (it has no link today)
findings.evidence: The open event exists only in React state (src/app/page.tsx:50, 105-106), so an event has no web address. There is no navigator.share or wa.me anywhere in src. The only copy-to-share flows are the monthly report link (src/app/quests/page.tsx:26) and the crew invite code (src/app/crew/page.tsx:179). The map loads every live event within 45 km and 45 days (src/lib/useEvents.ts:38, 41), and the card is found from the unfiltered list (page.tsx:106). So a link that names an event can open it with data already on the phone. The report share page is client-rendered (src/app/report/share/[token]/page.tsx), and nothing in src sets per-page preview metadata.
findings.why: Design §07 screen 04 calls the event page 'The most shared object in the product… Built to look right pasted into WhatsApp', and says the stub 'gives you a free shareable shape for WhatsApp'.
findings.suggestion: Give every event a link (for example, the map opening with ?e=<event id>, which pre-selects that event). Add a 'SHARE' button on the stub that opens the phone's share sheet with text like 'SOUTH SOCIAL · FRI 10 OCT · LEKKI · ₦10,000 · 23 Hoppers going' plus the link. The same link lets Discover's 'you're going' chips and any future Tonight list open this one event page. A proper WhatsApp preview card (image + title) needs a small server-rendered page per event; see the questions.
findings.gamification_angle: Every share is an invite, and invites fill the guest list you just stamped yourself onto.

findings.title: Cut the chat preview ('On the ground')
findings.evidence: There is already a chat icon in the header (EventCard.tsx:116-118). The scroll area repeats it with an 'On the ground / OPEN CHAT' header (235-241), then the last 6 messages (242-251, fetched in src/lib/useEventFeed.ts:35-40) with author names in orange (246). The empty state reads 'Nobody has said anything yet. Ask who's going.' (253).

findings.suggestion: Delete the preview. Keep a single quiet row below the fold, 'EVENT CHAT →' in mono, or just a labelled chat button in the secondary row next to TICKETS and SHARE.

findings.title: Move the flyer into the stub; hide the photo strip until there are photos
findings.evidence: EventCard.tsx:192-233. The flyer (flyer_url) is buried as the first thumbnail of 'Pictures from tonight' (224), below the quests, drops and chart. The heading says 'tonight' even for an event weeks away (194). Every event without photos shows the filler 'No pictures yet. Hoppers who check in can post them here.' (230-232). The 'ADD ONE' upload appears once you have checked in (195-220). Uploads go to review first (src/lib/useEventFeed.ts:74), and only approved photos can be read (supabase/schema.sql:480). Photo quests send people here to post (src/app/quests/page.tsx:35).
findings.why: The flyer is the best artwork on the page, and the draft puts artwork (Tier 4) inside the stub. Empty sections are noise on a screen that should do its job quietly.
findings.suggestion: The flyer becomes the art panel at the top of the stub; tapping it opens it full size. The photo strip appears only when approved photos exist, titled 'PHOTOS FROM THE NIGHT'. 'Add a photo' stays, as a small text link shown only after check-in, because photo quests depend on it. Delete the 'No pictures yet' line.

findings.title: Strip the header label, tag row and footnote down to at most one pill
findings.evidence: Source label at EventCard.tsx:91 (mapped at 18-23: 'Hoppaz pick', 'Dropped by a Hopper', 'From Instagram', 'Listing'). Tag row at 129-134: the vibe as an orange-bordered tag (tag-o, src/app/globals.css:54-56), 'HOP STOP' in violet (131, tag-v at globals.css:57-59), 'OUTSIDE YOUR N KM' (132), and 'N SAID THEY'RE IN' (133). Footnote at 256-260: 'Check-in opens inside 1.5 km of the venue, and the server checks it. You are X km out.' The checked-in button uses a text '✓' (114). The close button is 32px (h-8 w-8, line 88). The map already fades events outside your radius (globals.css:240-243).
findings.why: The draft allows 'One tier-2 colour per card, maximum', and pills are 'Mono caps, 1px border in the tier-2 colour, transparent fill'. An orange tag you can't tap breaks 'orange is a verb', and violet is reserved for 'Live drop, rare, legendary'. The source label is internal metadata, and 'the server checks it' is engineer copy.
findings.suggestion: Drop the source label, except on leads, which get one yellow (Danfo) pill: 'UNVERIFIED · CHECK LISTING'. The vibe becomes plain mono text in the stub line (e.g. 'AFROBEATS'). 'HOP STOP' becomes plain mono text, 'ON THE HOP ROUTE', with no violet. Remove 'OUTSIDE YOUR KM'. 'Said they're in' becomes the big guest-list number. The footnote becomes the button's own label when you're far: 'CHECK IN OPENS AT THE VENUE'. Make the close target 44px.

findings.title: Discover has a second, different event detail: make its info button open the same event page
findings.evidence: discover/page.tsx never opens EventCard. SwipeDeck's info button (SwipeDeck.tsx:118-125) expands a facts grid (185-219) that repeats the tags just above it. Gate fee repeats the price tag (176/188), Doors repeats the time tag (175/189), and Distance repeats 177/190. Then come Est. travel, Route, 'Saying they are in' (also HeatBar's label, 182/193), 'Checked in' and 'Listed by'. HeatBar (src/components/HeatBar.tsx:1-16) shows an abstract 'HEAT 73' in orange with a decorative orange gradient bar. 'SWIPE RIGHT IF YOU ARE IN…' is printed on every card (SwipeDeck.tsx:221-223). The 'You said you are in' chips can't be tapped (discover/page.tsx:113-130). The drag stamp is orange-bordered (SwipeDeck.tsx:160) and tilted 6° (rotate-6, 159).
findings.why: Two different detail views for the same event is unprofessional and doubles the design work. 'Heat' is an internal score, not a reason to go out. The numbers rule and the orange-is-a-verb rule apply here too. The draft's stamp 'rotates a degree or two off square', and 'going' is Keke green, not orange.
findings.suggestion: Make the deck card a compact ticket stub: title, one mono line, at most one pill, and the going count. The info button opens the same event page as the map, so the app has one event page. Cut HeatBar and the facts grid. Show the swipe instruction only on the first card of the first session. Make the 'you're going' chips tappable, opening that event page (this needs the event link from the share finding). Keep the drag stamp, but relabel it 'GOING' with a green border and text, tilted 1-2° instead of 6°. Keep 'NAH' in dim grey.
findings.gamification_angle: The stamp-on-swipe already feels like the brand, and it matches the stamp-your-face moment on the event page.

findings.title: Use one word for the same action: 'going', not 'in'
findings.evidence: The same 'in' swipe is labelled seven ways: the 'I'M IN' stamp (SwipeDeck.tsx:163), the 'I am in' aria label (128), the toast 'YOU ARE IN · …' (discover/page.tsx:52), 'You said you are in' (discover/page.tsx:115), 'N SAID THEY'RE IN' (EventCard.tsx:133), 'Saying they are in' (SwipeDeck.tsx:193) and 'N in' (SwipeDeck.tsx:182), plus 'SWIPE RIGHT IF YOU ARE IN' (222). Crew plans already store the status as 'going' (src/lib/game.ts:41) but the button reads 'I'M IN' (src/app/crew/page.tsx:181).
findings.why: The draft's lip button reads 'I'M GOING', and Keke green is defined as 'Going, confirmed, claimed'. Professional products use one verb per action.
findings.suggestion: Rename all of them to GOING: 'I'M GOING', 'YOU'RE GOING', '23 GOING', 'Where you're going', 'Swipe right if you're going'. Copy change only.
findings.gamification_angle: One verb builds one habit: 'going' is the thing you count.

findings.title: Day events should get the cream stub (card follows the event's time) and fonts/tokens should match the draft
findings.evidence: The card is always dark (bg-ink-2, EventCard.tsx:84) and the app is dark-only (globals.css:7). Tokens drift from the draft (tailwind.config.ts:12-18, duplicated for the map in src/lib/brand.ts:2-12): ink-2 #17110F, ink-3 #231915, dim #8A7C73 and line #2E211C, against the draft's #171210, #221A17, #9C9087 and #2E2320. There are no Keke, Lagoon, Danfo or Fire Ant tokens, and 'ok' is #49D07A where Keke is #2FD35C. Fonts loaded are Poppins 400/600/900 and Space Mono (src/app/layout.tsx:4-8; globals.css:8-9), with no Archivo or DM Mono. The body runs Poppins at its default 400 weight (globals.css:16), and body sentences use the mono .hint class (globals.css:66-68).
findings.why: 'Theme follows the clock. Card treatment follows the event.' A day event and a night event can sit side by side, each in its own treatment. Archivo is for 'Everything you read'. Mono is only for labels, dates and prices. Poppins is 'Never below 600 anywhere'.
findings.suggestion: Render the event stub on the cream day set (#FFFCF7 card on #F5EBDD) when the event starts in daytime Lagos hours (starts_at is already on the row), with a light-blue (Lagoon) 'DAYTIME' pill. Night events keep the night card. Switch body sentences to Archivo and dates, prices and labels to DM Mono (two new font packages; no back-end change). Align the night tokens to the draft values in both tailwind.config.ts and brand.ts, and add the tier-2 tokens so pills can use them.

findings.title: Restyle the Hop sheet as the original ticket stub and cut its repeated copy
findings.evidence: HopSheet.tsx has: the label 'The Hop · every two weeks' (20); an 18px title (21); a date formatted without the Lagos time zone (23-27, unlike dayLagos in geo.ts:108-115); a tagline (28) plus a second pitch paragraph (63-66); a violet 'THE BUS IS THE FIFTH PARTY' tag (31); boarding as an orange tag (32); stop numbers on solid violet and orange discs (41-46); and 'km from you' on every stop (52). The 'GET A SEAT' lip button (70-72) is good.

findings.suggestion: Show the Hop as a big stub: 'THE HOP', then a DM Mono line with date, price and boarding point (in Lagos time). Draw the stops as a vertical route line with stop times in mono and plain cream or hairline dots. Keep one sentence of copy and the 'GET A SEAT' lip button. Make 'Hop chat' a text link. Drop the per-stop distance.
findings.gamification_angle: A punched Hop stub is the collectible people keep on their Crew shelf.

findings.title: One sheet pattern, the draft's motion, the real lip-button spec, and no emoji in working UI
findings.evidence: EventCard is a floating card (EventCard.tsx:84: inset-x-3 bottom-3 max-h-[64%] animate-rise), as are FilterCard (FilterCard.tsx:40) and PersonCard (chat/PersonCard.tsx:64). The Hop and area pickers use Sheet (Sheet.tsx:37-38: full-width, border-t-2 border-orange). That is two overlay patterns, and the orange top edge is decoration. 'rise' slides in from 100% with no misregistration (tailwind.config.ts:34, 39). The .btn lip (globals.css:38-43) uses 'rounded' (4px radius), presses only 2px (active:translate-y-0.5) and keeps a 2px lip when pressed (active:shadow-chunk-sm; shadow-chunk is the 4px lip, tailwind.config.ts:27-28). Emoji in working UI: 🎁 (EventCard.tsx:142), collectible emoji (159), and 📸 ▦ ✦ (EventQuestList.tsx:52).
findings.why: Draft rules: 'Sheets rise with a violet copy offset six pixels for 120ms before snapping into place.' The lip button is 'Radius 6px' and 'On press the face translates down exactly 4px and the lip disappears.' Nothing orange is decorative, and the working UI is plain.
findings.suggestion: Use one sheet for the event page: taller (about 85%), with a grab handle and a hairline top edge instead of orange, rising with the violet misregistration. Tune the lip button to spec: 6px radius, a 4px press, and the lip vanishes. Replace emoji with the line icons the app already uses (lucide), or with collectible art where it exists.
findings.gamification_angle: The tactile 4px press on 'I'M GOING' is the physical half of the stamp moment.

findings.title: Check-in success has no moment: punch the stub, fly the badges, stop shouting a wrong XP number

Move the crew toggle into the filter sheet as 'Show my crew'. Show the bus button only on Hop night (see the Hop finding).
findings.gamification_angle: Rank changes still get their stamp moment on Me, and keeping XP off the map stops it becoming wallpaper.

findings.title: Theme follows the Lagos clock: add a cream day map
findings.evidence: The basemap is hard-wired to CARTO dark-matter (src/lib/mapStyle.ts:4-6) and the repaint only knows night colours (:19-89). The fallback style is night ink (:158-163). The page is locked to color-scheme dark (globals.css:7) with theme-color #0E0B0A (src/app/layout.tsx:28). Every HUD panel hard-codes night classes such as bg-ink-2/92 and text-cream (page.tsx:148, :204, :217, :237, :262, :281). The MapLibre controls and attribution are hard-coded dark (globals.css:79-97), as is the hover card (globals.css:263-275).
findings.why: The draft's first rule is 'Theme follows the clock': cream day ground, black night ground. For the map specifically it says 'Dark MapLibre tiles after sunset, light tiles before'.
findings.suggestion: Before sunset in Lagos (about 6:45pm), the map uses a cream ground and a light basemap; after sunset it switches to night. Chrome, sheets and markers use the draft's day and night token sets. Heat stays orange on both, a touch stronger on cream so it holds contrast. Engineers: CARTO publishes a light 'positron' style built the same way as dark-matter. Check that its layer ids match the repaint rules at mapStyle.ts:19-89, pass a day palette into repaint(), switch with map.setStyle at the boundary, and re-add the Hoppaz layers. Move the HUD and globals.css map colours to CSS variables. Open point: should the map follow the clock, or the night being browsed? (See questions.)
findings.gamification_angle: The map turning to night at sunset becomes a free daily ritual.

findings.title: Colour discipline: inert orange, off-palette browns and token drift
findings.evidence: Basemap 'orange arteries' (described at mapStyle.ts:13-17): motorways #D88A4E, bridges #C85E28, roads #896B56 (:55-77). The radius ring has an orange dashed line and a 4% orange fill and is never tappable (NightMap.tsx:235-253). Pin colours are the off-palette #2C2017 and #6E4433 (:317-319). Billboard meta text is ember (globals.css:218-220). Orange is used as status text in 'N POPPING' (page.tsx:240) and the radius readout (:276). Token drift against the draft: ink2 #17110F vs #171210, ink3 #231915 vs #221A17, line #2E211C vs #2E2320, dim #8A7C73 vs #9C9087, and 'ok' #49D07A vs Keke #2FD35C (tailwind.config.ts:12-18; src/lib/brand.ts:3-12). Fonts: Space Mono instead of DM Mono, no Archivo, and Poppins 400 loaded and used as body text (layout.tsx:4-8; globals.css:9, :16).
findings.why: Tier 1 orange must only mean 'act'. Tier 2 colours are one per card and never a surface. Grounds come only from Tier 3. Right now roads, the ring and the counters all borrow orange, so nothing on the map stands out as tappable.
findings.suggestion: Roads and bridges move to neutral ground tones (Tier 3 hairline and dim), so the only orange on the map is heat plus things you can tap. Status counters become plain cream text. Align the tokens in tailwind.config.ts and brand.ts with the draft's exact night and day values. Switch labels, dates and prices to DM Mono and body copy to Archivo, so the map chrome matches the other tabs.
findings.gamification_angle: When orange is rare, every orange thing becomes an invitation, which is the whole game loop.

findings.title: Hop route and bus: show only on Hop night, stop the bob, not violet, never show the demo hop live
findings.evidence: A violet route line, violet numbered stops and labels are drawn whenever a Hop exists (NightMap.tsx:255-289). The bus marker is orange with a violet border, sits on a violet label surface (:716-722), and bobs forever while 'moving' (globals.css:277-292). Its position is a schedule estimate ('There is no GPS on the bus yet, so this is an estimate', src/lib/busPosition.ts:6-10). Before the hop date it waits at stop 1 with the date (:43-50). After the date it parks at the finale saying 'NEXT HOP SOON' forever (:51-53). useHop() starts as DEMO_HOP (src/lib/useEvents.ts:93) and only replaces it when an announced or selling hop with stops is found (:100-123). So with no real hop, a production build shows the demo 'HOP 02 · FREEDOM' route (src/lib/demoData.ts:60-74, id 'demo-hop' at :61, dated 2026-10-09 at :63). From 10 Oct 2026 that means a permanently parked 'NEXT HOP SOON' bus. The bus HUD button is at page.tsx:177-186.
findings.why: The draft reserves violet for 'live drop, rare, legendary. Scarcity only' and says 'Tier 2 never paints a surface'. A permanent violet route plus an animated bus whose position is a guess is clutter and motion on six nights out of seven. Showing a demo hop to real users is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Show the Hop route, stops, bus and bus button only when the selected night is the Hop's night; every other night they are gone. Draw the route as a plain cream dashed line with numbered stop stubs. Take the bob away. Give the bus a card-coloured label 'EST. · → STOP 3', so nobody waits on a guess. Engineers: these are display conditions in page.tsx (compare hop.hop_date with the selected night, and skip rendering when hop.id is 'demo-hop' outside demo mode). Flag the DEMO_HOP initial state (useEvents.ts:93) to whoever owns data, since changing that is logic, not UI.
findings.gamification_angle: On Hop night, the route appearing on the map becomes an event in itself.

findings.title: Everything that moves on the map, and what should stop
findings.evidence: (1) Every billboard pops in on an overshoot spring, cubic-bezier(.34,1.8,.64,1), staggered 0.06 s by rank (globals.css:208-212; NightMap.tsx:592). It replays for any sign that is removed and recreated after a filter change (:578-634). (2) The bus bobs forever (globals.css:281-292). (3) The city grows with an overshoot (mapStyle.ts:141-151). (4) The 3.4 s swoop on every mount (NightMap.tsx:779-797). (5) Camera eases of 700-1600 ms on recentre (:807), filter-fit (:677), event tap (:689-695) and bus tap (:744). (6) The filter card and event card slide up with animate-rise (FilterCard.tsx:40; EventCard.tsx:84; tailwind.config.ts:34, :39). (7) The heat changes with no transition at all (NightMap.tsx:392-400), which is the one place the draft wants motion. The reduced-motion CSS (globals.css:294-302) does not reach the requestAnimationFrame city rise.
findings.why: The draft says 'Everywhere else, nothing moves', 'stamp, not bounce (180ms, hard ease-out, no elastic overshoot)', and 'misregistration, not fade' for sheets. On the map, 'the only ambient motion' is the heat bloom.
findings.suggestion: Markers simply appear, with no pop and no spring. Remove the bus bob, the city grow and the swoop. Keep camera moves only when the person asked for them (tapped an event, changed the night), short and mostly flat. When the filter card or event card opens, use the draft's misregistration: a violet copy offset 6px for about 120ms, then it snaps into place. Spend the whole motion budget on the heat bloom while scrubbing.
findings.gamification_angle: Restraint is what makes the heat bloom, and later the Drop reveal, feel special.

findings.title: Status messages on the map: engineer copy and off-palette colours
findings.evidence: page.tsx:226-230 shows 'DEMO NIGHT · NOT CONNECTED TO THE DATABASE' or 'LIVE EVENT DATA UNAVAILABLE · CHECK DATABASE SETUP' in off-palette #A98CFF with a violet border. page.tsx:231-235 shows 'PRODUCTION DATABASE NOT CONFIGURED · LIVE EVENTS UNAVAILABLE' in orange. The empty-filter message 'Nothing on for that. / Try another night or fewer types.' floats mid-map (page.tsx:215-222). A reload function already exists (useEvents.ts:89), but page.tsx:43 does not use it. Pull-to-refresh is blocked by overscroll-behavior: none (globals.css:18).
findings.why: Database setup copy in front of a Lagos raver reads unfinished. Errors belong to Fire Ant (#E5484D), not orange or violet; violet is scarcity only.
findings.suggestion: Users never see the words 'database' or 'production'. In test builds, show a small dim mono 'SAMPLE NIGHT' tag. If live events cannot load, show one plain line with a Fire Ant dot: 'Can't reach tonight's events.' plus a 'TRY AGAIN' text button wired to the existing reload (tiny hookup, no new logic). Keep the 'Nothing on for that' empty state, which has good voice. With the night rail, most empty results disappear, because '0 on' nights are visible before you pick them.

findings.title: The + button: rename it away from 'Drop', and make it a real lip button
findings.evidence: page.tsx:296-303: a round orange FAB (rounded-full) linking to /drop, labelled 'Drop a flyer on the map'. The target page heading is 'Drop a flyer' (src/app/drop/page.tsx:105). On press it moves 2px and keeps a 2px lip (active:translate-y-0.5 active:shadow-chunk-sm). Its position is hard-coded at bottom-[178px].
findings.why: In the design system 'Drop' means the sealed-box reward reveal, so 'drop a flyer' muddies the most important word in the game. The draft's lip button is radius 6 (rough and square, not round) and 'on press the face translates down exactly 4px and the lip disappears'.
findings.suggestion: Rename the action to 'Post a night' (or 'Add event'; see questions), so 'drop' only ever means rewards. Restyle it as a square-ish lip button: radius 6, a 4px ember edge, and on press it travels 4px with no lip left. It sits just above the time scrubber.
findings.gamification_angle: Keeping 'drop' sacred makes every real drop feel like an event.

findings.title: Keep: the smart decluttering, desktop hover card, crew opt-in and fit-to-results
findings.evidence: The billboard declutter ranks signs (selected, then in range, then heat) and steps them down from full to price tag to hidden so they never pile up (NightMap.tsx:480-518, :569-576). The desktop-only hover peek (matchMedia hover check at :524) uses textContent for safety (:520-556) and shows travel time and 'over the bridge' (:539-545). Crew faces are off by default (src/lib/store.ts:38) behind a toggle (page.tsx:187-199). The map frames whatever matches when filters change (NightMap.tsx:667-680).
findings.why: These do real work quietly, which is what the draft asks of the working layer. They should survive the restyle, not be rebuilt.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the declutter for the new stub markers (full stub, then mini stub with the price, then dot). Restyle the hover card with the stub look and the day/night tokens. Keep crew as opt-in, moved into the filter sheet. When the night rail changes night, keep auto-framing the map to that night's events.

findings.title: First-run intro: keep it as the loud moment, but tighten it and land on a flat, quiet map
findings.evidence: src/components/TitleSequence.tsx:22-24 runs 0.5 s + 9 s pan + 2.2 s, about 11.7 s, with a SKIP button (:382-387). Reduced-motion users skip it (:113-116). It uses spring overshoot on buildings and signs (globals.css:110-119), an infinite star twinkle (globals.css:137-139; TitleSequence.tsx:255) and a violet moon (:258). Its buildings have orange caps and windows (:147, :154), which is fine as Tier 4 artwork. The final wordmark 'stamp' is 0.5 s with an elastic overshoot, cubic-bezier(.34,1.7,.64,1) (:367). The README says it hands off to a swoop 'into a pitched 3D city' (README.md:149-150), but the swoop actually lands at zoom 11.2-12.2 (NightMap.tsx:791), below the zoom-13 city. It plays once per install (page.tsx:87, :332).
findings.why: First run is explicitly a loud-layer moment in the draft, so the intro is allowed. But 'stamp, not bounce (180ms, hard ease-out, no elastic overshoot)' still applies, and it should hand off cleanly to the new quiet map.
findings.suggestion: Keep the intro as the one cinematic first impression, cut to about 6 seconds. Swap the springy pops and the 0.5 s elastic wordmark for the draft's 180ms hard stamp. The flat map is simply there on Tonight afterwards, with no swoop. First run is an allowed place for the mascot, for example waving as the wordmark lands, if Jae wants it.
findings.gamification_angle: A short, confident opener sets the 'this is a game' tone without making the map itself noisy.

questions_for_jae: You said 3D only where events are. Proposal: one small 3D object per event, shaped like the ticket stub (cheap, built in code), and a violet sealed box for events with a live drop. No other 3D anywhere, and the Sims houses and the orange city go. Is that right, or do you want a custom-modelled object instead (needs a 3D artist and more engineering)?
Should the map open on Tonight every time, and jump to the next night that has events when tonight has none? Can 'Any day' be removed as an option?

The Hop bus and route are violet today, but the draft reserves violet for drops only. What colour should the Hop be, and is it OK to show it only on Hop night? Also: today, with no real hop announced, the live app shows a demo hop dated 9 Oct. Who should fix that on the data side?
Day/night switch: should the map follow the real Lagos clock (cream before about 6:45pm), or the night you are browsing (for example Saturday shown dark even at noon)?
Is it OK to remove the XP/level chip from the map and leave numbers to the Me tab? This depends on the draft's open question about which two currencies are visible.
Can the tilted HOPPAZ wordmark leave the map's top bar (to make room for the night rail) and live only on the intro, the install sheet and share cards?
Radius: keep it as a feature, but set it in the location sheet with four plain choices (walkable / my side / across the bridge / all Lagos) instead of the 2-40 km slider on the map?
The + button says 'Drop a flyer', but in the design system 'Drop' means the sealed-box reward. Can we rename the flyer action ('Post a night' or 'Add event') so 'drop' only means rewards?
Should crew faces stay on the map at all (off by default today), or live only in the Crew tab?
Map empty state: the draft allows the mascot in empty states but bans it from the map. Which rule wins for 'Nothing on for that'?
Intro: keep the roughly 12-second animated city opener, cut it to about 6 seconds, or replace it with a mascot first-run moment?

verify:dates-tonight.surface: Date selection + Tonight (Discover) feed: src/lib/filters.ts, src/components/FilterCard.tsx, src/app/discover/page.tsx, src/components/SwipeDeck.tsx, src/components/HeatBar.tsx, src/lib/useEvents.ts, src/lib/store.ts, src/lib/crowd.ts (time strip), and the filter and time-strip parts of src/app/page.tsx
verify:dates-tonight.current_state_summary: A "night" runs from 6am to 6am Lagos time, so a party starting at 1am Saturday counts as Friday night (filters.ts:6-7, 13-15). The date choices are ANY DAY, THIS WEEKEND, TONIGHT, TOMORROW and five more weekday chips, covering 7 nights (filters.ts:24-42), plus a native phone date picker with no limits (FilterCard.tsx:68-77, discover/page.tsx:97-106). The app loads events from 4 hours ago up to 45 days ahead (schema.sql:232, useEvents.ts:41). The chosen date is shared between Map and Tonight, but it resets to "ANY DAY" on every launch (store.ts:48, 55-59), so both screens open on about six weeks of events mixed together. Map pins show a clock time with no date (NightMap.tsx:646-647). On the Map, the date lives two taps deep behind a sliders icon (page.tsx:164-176), and a summary pill appears only once you change it (page.tsx:202-213). The TONIGHT tab is a page titled "Discover" (discover/page.tsx:69) holding a one-card-at-a-time swipe deck sorted by distance (discover/page.tsx:43). Any card you swipe is hidden from that tab for good (discover/page.tsx:29-31, 41), the deck is the only place a Hopper can say "I'm in" (the only swipes write is at discover/page.tsx:56-58), and there is no event page to open from Tonight (src/app has no event route).

findings.title: Default to a real night, not 'Any day' across 45 days
findings.evidence: store.ts:48 sets dateFilter: ANY_DATE, and store.ts:55-59 deliberately leaves it out of what is saved, so every launch starts on 'any'. useEvents.ts:41 loads events up to 45 days ahead, and p_from defaults to now minus 4h (schema.sql:232). page.tsx:55-58 and discover/page.tsx:38-45 then show all of them. BottomNav.tsx:10 names the tab TONIGHT. Map billboard text is price, clock time and minutes away, with no date (NightMap.tsx:646-647). Only the hover peek shows the day (NightMap.tsx:537), and it is limited to devices with a mouse (NightMap.tsx:524). The 'clear' paths also go back to 'any': clearFilters at page.tsx:60-63, used by the pill's x at page.tsx:208 and by CLEAR in FilterCard.tsx:108-110. page.tsx:59 treats 'any' as 'no filter'.
findings.why: This is the root cause of 'dates feel broken'. A party six weeks away looks exactly like tonight's on the map and in the deck. The design draft says nobody going out picks a range; they pick 'Friday'. A tab named TONIGHT that opens on every night for six weeks reads as unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Every screen always has exactly one night selected. When the app opens, select Tonight. If tonight has nothing on, select the next night that has events. Remove 'ANY DAY' as an option. CLEAR in the filter sheet and the x on the pill should only clear 'what kind'; the night is never cleared. Keep the current rule that the date is forgotten when the app closes. Engineering: change the starting value in the store (store.ts:48), pick the first night with events once they load, and stop clearFilters (page.tsx:60-63) resetting the date. All of this is screen state; no back-end change.
findings.gamification_angle: With one night selected, the conductor line ('23 Hoppers out') and the 'N on' counts read as live and urgent rather than as a catalogue.

findings.title: Build the Night Rail as one shared date control
findings.evidence: There are two separate copies of the date UI today. FilterCard.tsx:50-77 is a wrapping grid of chips plus 'Choose another date'. discover/page.tsx:80-106 is a scrolling row of round chips plus 'Pick a date', and works out which chip is selected with its own code at lines 86-88 instead of the dateKey helper FilterCard uses (FilterCard.tsx:33, filters.ts:44). Both read dateOptions(), which only goes 7 nights ahead (filters.ts:30). Chip text is 9-10px Space Mono (discover/page.tsx:87, FilterCard.tsx:59, globals.css:9). The shared state already exists: dateFilter and setDateFilter (store.ts:27-29). Per-night counts can be worked out from the events already loaded, using nightOf() (filters.ts:13). Today three different 'how many' numbers exist for the same filter: the map pill uses events.length (page.tsx:206), the radius row counts only events inside the radius (page.tsx:277), and Tonight counts unswiped cards (discover/page.tsx:71).
findings.why: The design draft makes the Night Rail the primary date control: 14 nights in a horizontal row, each showing weekday, date and 'N on', with a month grid hidden behind a calendar icon. Today's chips have no counts, so you can't see which nights are busy without tapping each one. Two copies of one control will drift apart, and they already have.
findings.suggestion: Build one 'Night Rail' and use it on both Map and Tonight. It is a horizontal row of 14 square tiles. Each tile has a small mono weekday on top (the first tile says TONIGHT), a big Poppins Black date number in the middle, and a small mono 'N on' underneath. The selected tile is solid orange with the dark ember lip and presses down like the lip button. Tiles with 0 events are dimmed but still tappable. A small calendar icon at the end opens the month grid in the existing bottom sheet (Sheet.tsx). The grid only lets you pick dates from today to 45 days out, the range the app actually loads, with a dot under busy dates. 'N on' should be one number used everywhere: events that night matching the 'what kind' filter, the same count the map pill shows today. Make the rail a real radio group, so a screen reader hears 'Friday 9 October, 23 events'. No label smaller than 11px.
findings.gamification_angle: '23 on' next to Friday works like a scoreboard. It makes busy nights look hot and builds anticipation for the weekend. Big date numbers follow the 'numbers are display type' rule.

findings.title: Put the rail on the Map so the date is always visible
findings.evidence: On the Map, the date only lives inside the sliders-icon sheet (page.tsx:164-176 opens FilterCard at page.tsx:320-330). The summary pill appears only when a filter is on (page.tsx:202-213), so on the default 'any' the map gives no hint of which night you're looking at. The map already re-frames the camera when the date changes (fitKey at page.tsx:134, NightMap.tsx:667-680). The top row is already busy with the wordmark, XP chip, sliders, bus and crew buttons (page.tsx:142-200).
findings.why: Jae wants the date always settable and visible. Today it is two taps deep and invisible by default. The design gives the map a time scrubber at the bottom, which only makes sense once a night has been picked.
findings.suggestion: Put a slim version of the Night Rail across the top of the map, below the wordmark row: about 44px tall, roughly 6 tiles visible. It takes the place of the orange filter pill. Picking a night on Tonight shows that night on the Map, and the other way round, because the choice is already shared. The sliders button then only holds 'What kind', so rename its sheet 'What kind' and delete its 'When' section. The rule to remember: the night at the top, the hour at the bottom. If the top row is too crowded, fall back to one always-visible chip, 'FRI 9 · 23 ON', that opens the full rail when tapped. Never hide the date completely.
findings.gamification_angle: Flicking between nights while the map re-frames and the orange heat fades in and out is the 'scrub the city' feel the design describes.

findings.title: Replace the swipe deck with a ticket-stub list ordered by Hoppers going
findings.evidence: discover/page.tsx:110 renders SwipeDeck, which shows one card at a time (SwipeDeck.tsx:26-27). The list is sorted by distance (discover/page.tsx:43), not by people going. Every swiped event is hidden from Tonight for good: judged is filled from the saved swipes (discover/page.tsx:29-31) and filtered out at line 41. There is no undo. The going count already exists as swipes_in on every event (types.ts:17), counted from 'in' swipes (schema.sql:212, 218). The deck's 'I'm in' is the only way to say you're going: the only swipes write is discover/page.tsx:56-58, and the map's EventCard only offers check-in (EventCard.tsx:112-115). The fling motion is a 520px fly-off with a 16-degree spin (SwipeDeck.tsx:61, 75) plus a drag tilt (SwipeDeck.tsx:58).
findings.why: The design's Tonight screen is the night rail, then stubs ordered by how many Hoppers are going. A one-at-a-time deck can't answer 'what's the best thing on Friday?', because that needs options side by side. One accidental left swipe removes a party from your Tonight tab forever. The fling motion breaks the rule that nothing moves outside the drop reveal.
findings.suggestion: Make Tonight a plain scrolling list of ticket stubs for the selected night. Each stub is the dark card with two punched half-circle notches on the sides. Order: most people going first, then earliest start time. Show every event, including ones you swiped before. Each stub has a small 'I'M GOING' lip button that saves what a right swipe saves today (see the 'I'm going' saving finding for one wiring catch). Tapping the stub body opens the event (see the finding about Tonight having nowhere to open an event). There is no 'pass' in the main view. Delete the deck controls (SwipeDeck.tsx:109-133) and the 'SWIPE RIGHT IF YOU ARE IN' line (SwipeDeck.tsx:221-223). If Jae wants to keep swiping as a game, it can live behind a small 'Can't decide? Swipe tonight' link, for the selected night only. Its cards must then be stubs too: the draft lists 'a card in the deck' as a stub.
findings.gamification_angle: Ordering by people going turns the list into a live leaderboard of the night. 'I'm going' becomes the main action and feeds the heat on the map, so every tap visibly counts.

findings.title: Cards print the calendar day, but the filter uses the 'night'
findings.evidence: The filter treats 6am to 6am as one night, so a 1am Saturday start counts as Friday (filters.ts:6-7, 13-15, 60). The cards print the plain calendar day with dayLagos() (geo.ts:108-115): the swipe card (SwipeDeck.tsx:167), the event card header (EventCard.tsx:94) and the map hover peek (NightMap.tsx:537). Pick 'FRI 9' and a midnight or 1am party in the list is labelled 'Sat, 10 Oct'.
findings.why: Users will read this as a bug, and it undermines trust in the date filter, which is exactly what Jae asked to fix. Lagos parties starting at midnight or later are common, so this will show up often.
findings.suggestion: Wherever a stub or card prints a date, print the night it belongs to, then the time. For example 'FRI 9 OCT · 11PM', and for after-midnight starts 'FRI NIGHT · 1AM'. The helper that knows the night, nightOf(), already exists. Only the text formatting changes.

findings.title: Remove the native phone date pickers
findings.evidence: FilterCard.tsx:68-77 ('Choose another date') and discover/page.tsx:97-106 ('Pick a date') use <input type=date> with no min or max, and force [color-scheme:dark] (FilterCard.tsx:75, discover/page.tsx:104). Events only exist from now minus 4 hours (schema.sql:232) to 45 days ahead (useEvents.ts:41). Picking yesterday or two months out silently shows 'Nothing on for that' on the Map (page.tsx:215-222), or 'That is the whole night' on Tonight (SwipeDeck.tsx:44-55). Pick a date beyond the 7 chips on Tonight and no chip is highlighted; the only sign of which night you're on is the native box (discover/page.tsx:86-88, 102). The Drop-a-flyer form uses the same native picker (drop/page.tsx:162).
findings.why: The phone's own calendar (an iOS wheel, the Android Material sheet) is the least on-brand thing in the app. It ignores the day/night theme rule and lets people pick dates the app has no data for. On Tonight it also takes up a permanent row above the content.
findings.suggestion: Delete both 'Pick a date' and 'Choose another date' rows. The rail covers the next 14 nights, and the calendar icon's month grid covers planning further ahead, with only loadable dates selectable. Optional, later: use the same month grid in the Drop-a-flyer form so posting and browsing share one calendar.

findings.title: Make the heat time strip follow the chosen night
findings.evidence: The selected time slot starts at 0 ('NOW', live) and is never reset when the date changes (page.tsx:76-77). Pick Friday on a Thursday and the strip still says 'Heat · live from check-ins' and 'QUIET RIGHT NOW' (page.tsx:239-241). With the 'any' default, timeSlots() centres the strip on the middle start time of every loaded event, up to 45 days of them (crowd.ts:53-61), which can be weeks away. It labels that point with only a weekday, like 'SAT 11PM' (crowd.ts:68-69).
findings.why: The bottom strip is meant to answer 'what time on this night'. Right now it can quietly point at a different night than the one you picked, and its labels don't say which Saturday.
findings.suggestion: Once one night is always selected (first finding), the strip already centres on that night, because it is fed the filtered list (page.tsx:75). What's left is screen-only. When the night changes, jump back to the first slot. If the night is tonight, keep NOW first. If it is a future night, hide NOW and the 'live from check-ins' wording, start at that night's first expected hour, and put one small label like 'FRI 9' at the left end.
findings.gamification_angle: Picking a night, then dragging through its hours to watch the heat bloom, is the map's one allowed ambient motion. It only works if both controls agree.

findings.title: Show the 'what kind' filter on Tonight and restyle the vibe chips
findings.evidence: Tonight silently applies the vibe types chosen on the Map (discover/page.tsx:15, 41), but has no control or indicator for them. The types are remembered across launches; only the date is left out (store.ts:55-59). The vibe chips are round, Poppins Black, with a solid orange fill (FilterCard.tsx:88-100).
findings.why: Pick 'techno' on the map last week and Tonight quietly hides everything else today, with no explanation. The design's pills are mono caps with a 1px border and no fill, not filled orange blobs.
findings.suggestion: When any types are on, show them as a slim row of removable pills under the rail, on both Map and Tonight (for example 'AMAPIANO x'), plus a 'clear' link. Restyle the chips in the 'What kind' sheet as design-system pills: mono caps, thin border, see-through. Selected: orange border and orange text. Unselected: hairline border and dim text.

findings.title: Rename to Tonight, cut the duplicate MAP button, add the conductor line
findings.evidence: The page heading says 'Discover' (discover/page.tsx:69) while the tab says TONIGHT (BottomNav.tsx:10). A 'MAP' ghost button (discover/page.tsx:74-76) repeats the bottom nav. The subline '{deck.length} events' (discover/page.tsx:70-72) counts unswiped cards, so it shrinks as you swipe. The data for a live line already exists: here_now, check-ins in the last 3 hours (types.ts:18-19, schema.sql:220); swipes_in (types.ts:17); and useCollectibleEventIds() for events with a drop (useCollectibles.ts:49-63, already used by the Map at page.tsx:44). That hook returns events that have a drop (old collectibles or live game drops, useCollectibles.ts:57-58), not a count of drops.
findings.why: Mismatched names and duplicate navigation read as unfinished. The design asks for one live line at the very top of Tonight, in the conductor's voice.
findings.suggestion: Heading in big Poppins Black: 'Tonight' when tonight is selected, otherwise the weekday ('Friday'). Delete the MAP button. Replace the count with one live sentence. Tonight: '23 Hoppers out. Drops at 2 spots.' (recent check-ins, plus events with a drop). A future night: 'Friday: 41 going. Drops at 1 spot.' Leave out the drop part when there are none. Use cream text, not orange, because the line isn't tappable. Engineering: add the same drops hook the Map uses to the Tonight page. It's existing data.
findings.gamification_angle: A conductor-voice line makes the city feel populated, and it is the screen's one allowed gamified moment in the draft.

findings.title: Slim each event down to a stub: cut the heat bar, fact grid and extra tags
findings.evidence: Each swipe card stacks: a date label, the title, the venue, 3-4 tags (vibe, time, price, km; SwipeDeck.tsx:173-178), a HeatBar with orange 'HEAT 72' text over a gradient bar (HeatBar.tsx:4-9, used only by SwipeDeck.tsx:180-183), and an info panel of 8 facts: gate fee, doors, distance, est. travel, route, 'saying they are in', checked in, listed by (SwipeDeck.tsx:185-219). The vibe tag is orange but can't be tapped (SwipeDeck.tsx:174, globals.css:54-56). All tags are 8.5px (globals.css:50-53). 'Heat' mixes in a seeded base score that isn't real people (schema.sql:213).
findings.why: The design's stub is: the title, one mono line with date, area and price, and a pill or two. The heat bar puts orange on text you can't tap and uses a gradient, which breaks the 'orange is a verb' and 'flat' rules. The fact grid repeats the event card, and 8.5px text is too small to read on a phone at night.
findings.suggestion: Stub layout: TITLE in Poppins Black, then one mono line, 'FRI 9 OCT · 11PM · LEKKI · ₦10,000', then pills, at least 11px. At most one coloured pill per stub. Green 'N GOING' is the default, hidden at 0 so a new event doesn't say '0 GOING'. Violet 'DROP' if the event has a drop. Yellow 'UNCONFIRMED' for unverified leads. Blue 'DAYTIME' for events starting before evening, which also get the cream day-card look ('card follows the event's own time'). Remove the HeatBar component from the list, plus the km, travel, route, listed-by and checked-in facts. Distance can come back as a small dim mono suffix if Jae wants it.
findings.gamification_angle: One loud number (people going) per stub reads as a scoreboard. Fewer competing numbers help it land.

findings.title: Empty states: mascot only on an empty night, plus 'jump to next busy night'
findings.evidence: SwipeDeck.tsx:44-55 says 'That is the whole night… tonight's list' even when another night, or 'any', is selected. It mentions the map and dropping a flyer but gives no button for either. The Map's message 'Nothing on for that. Try another night or fewer types.' (page.tsx:215-222) has no action either, and only appears when a filter is on (page.tsx:215). The repo has no mascot artwork yet: no file in src/ or public/ mentions 'mascot'.
findings.why: Empty states are one of the few places the draft allows the mascot ('on a quiet Tuesday only, as the empty state'). Today they are dead ends with the wrong copy.
findings.suggestion: Tonight, when the selected night has 0 events: show the mascot in its 'sleep' pose, the line 'Quiet one.', an orange lip button 'NEXT BUSY NIGHT · FRI 9 · 23 ON' that moves the rail there, and a quiet 'Drop a flyer' link to /drop. Use the mascot only when the night is completely empty. The draft bans it from the event list and from scrolling screens, so a night with 2-3 events shows them normally, with a plain text line at the bottom pointing to the next busy night. Map: no mascot (banned there). Same text and the same 'next busy night' button. The 'sleep' pose has to be exported from the mascot rig first.
findings.gamification_angle: The mascot dozing on a dead night is personality at the edge of the app, exactly where the draft wants it. The button keeps people moving instead of leaving.

findings.title: Remove the 'You said you are in' footer and toast; mark going in place
findings.evidence: The footer list lives only in this session's memory (discover/page.tsx:21, 51, 113-130), so it is empty again after a reload even though the swipes were saved. Its chips have orange borders but can't be tapped (discover/page.tsx:118-121), which breaks 'orange means tappable'. Swiping right also fires a cream toast, 'YOU ARE IN · TITLE' (discover/page.tsx:52, Toaster.tsx:17). The saved swipes are already fetched with their decision (discover/page.tsx:29), but only the IDs are used (line 31). Swipes are private to each Hopper (schema.sql:432-434), so the app can't show who else is going.
findings.why: The draft says 'I'm going' stamps your face onto the guest list in place, without navigating anywhere. A footer that forgets your choices, plus a toast, is the opposite.
findings.suggestion: Delete the footer and the toast. When you tap I'M GOING, the button stamps over to a green 'YOU'RE GOING' state (a 180ms stamp, no bounce), and your own avatar appears on that stub next to the going count. The avatar is already loaded; the map uses it at page.tsx:128. On reload, rebuild the going state from the swipes already fetched: the decision field is in the response, so this is a small hookup with no new query. A row of other people's faces would need new data, because swipes are private. That is a back-end question for Jae, not part of this pass.
findings.gamification_angle: The stamp is a small reward that sticks, and seeing your own face on the stub is the social hook.

findings.title: Fix the TOMORROW and THIS WEEKEND labels
findings.evidence: After midnight, the first option is still the night that started the evening before, labelled TONIGHT, and option 1 is always 'TOMORROW' (filters.ts:34-37). At 2am Saturday, 'TOMORROW' therefore means Saturday night, which in everyday speech is 'tonight'. THIS WEEKEND is a separate chip that selects the coming Fri/Sat/Sun nights, and on a Sunday selects only Sunday (filters.ts:47-56).
findings.why: Relative words like 'tomorrow' cause most date mistakes. Rail tiles with a weekday and a date number remove the ambiguity.
findings.suggestion: Rail tiles say only 'TONIGHT' or a weekday, never 'TOMORROW'. Between midnight and 6am, the first tile stays 'TONIGHT' and the next one shows its weekday ('SAT'). If Jae wants to keep the weekend shortcut, show a thin mono 'WEEKEND' bracket over the Fri/Sat/Sun tiles that selects all three, reusing the existing weekend filter. Otherwise drop it.
findings.gamification_angle: A weekend bracket over Fri-Sun quietly sets up the 'weekend streak' number on the Me tab.

findings.title: Show unverified 'LEAD' events as one pill, not a title prefix and five phrasings
findings.evidence: The 'LEAD · ' marker is stored inside the title (geo.ts:78-79), and eventTitle() already strips it (geo.ts:82-84). The UI then pastes it back in the deck (SwipeDeck.tsx:168), the footer (discover/page.tsx:122) and the map signs (NightMap.tsx:533, 598). The missing time and price appear as 'VERIFY DETAILS' (SwipeDeck.tsx:175), 'CHECK LISTING' and 'LEAD' (geo.ts:86-92), 'CHECK DETAILS' (NightMap.tsx:537, 647), 'Check event details' (discover/page.tsx:124), 'Check event listing' (SwipeDeck.tsx:189), 'check event listing for time' (EventCard.tsx:94) and 'Community lead · verify details' (EventCard.tsx:91).
findings.why: 'LEAD' is internal jargon, and a stack of phrasings for one idea looks messy. The draft's warning colour (Danfo yellow) exists for exactly this kind of heads-up.
findings.suggestion: Show the clean title. Add one yellow-bordered 'UNCONFIRMED' pill, which counts as that stub's one coloured pill. Use one phrase everywhere for the missing time: 'TIME TBC'. Keep 'see listing' as a link inside the event card only.

findings.title: The selected night goes stale if the app stays open past 6am
findings.evidence: The chosen night is held in memory as a fixed date (filters.ts:20, store.ts:48-50), while the chips work out 'tonight' fresh from the clock every time they draw (filters.ts:25, discover/page.tsx:82). useEvents refreshes the data when the app comes back to the foreground (useEvents.ts:62-72), but nothing moves the selected night forward. A phone that keeps the app open from Friday into Saturday afternoon stays on Friday's date. That night has dropped off the chip row, so no chip is highlighted (discover/page.tsx:86-88), and the list shows only leftovers from the last 4 hours (schema.sql:232).
findings.why: Once the app always opens on one night (first finding), this becomes the most common way it shows the wrong night. Mobile browsers and installed apps often keep a page alive for days.
findings.suggestion: When the app comes back to the foreground, if the selected night is now in the past, snap the rail to Tonight. This piggybacks on the foreground refresh that already exists, and it's screen state only.

findings.title: Tonight has nowhere to open an event
findings.evidence: There is no event page: src/app has no event route, only admin, chat, collection, community, crew, discover, drop, drops, me, privacy and quests. On the Map, the open event is local screen state (page.tsx:50) with no link to it. On Tonight, tapping a card does nothing; the info button only expands facts in place (SwipeDeck.tsx:118-125, 185-219). From Tonight you can't reach check-in, the event chat, drops or photos, which all live in EventCard (EventCard.tsx:112-167).
findings.why: A stub list needs a tap target, and the draft treats the event page as the most-shared object in the product. Right now Tonight is a dead end for anything except swiping.
findings.suggestion: Short term, UI only: tapping a stub opens the existing event card over the Tonight list. EventCard takes plain inputs (EventCard.tsx:30-49), and the check-in hook it needs already exists (page.tsx:47). Another option is a 'SEE ON MAP' action that opens the Map with that event selected; the map already flies to the selected event (NightMap.tsx:685-698), so it only needs to read the event from the link. The full event page from the draft (big stub, lineup, guest list, WhatsApp-shareable) is a separate build.

findings.title: Saving 'I'm going' must handle past swipes and only confirm after it saves
findings.evidence: onDecide saves with an upsert (discover/page.tsx:56-58). The swipes table allows insert and delete for your own rows but has no update permission (schema.sql:433-439). Changing an earlier 'pass' to 'in' would be refused, and the error is only logged to the console (discover/page.tsx:59). This never happens today, because judged events never come back (discover/page.tsx:41). The toast 'YOU ARE IN' fires before the save (line 52), and still fires when there is no signed-in user, in which case nothing is saved at all (line 55; anonymous sign-in can fail, useSession.ts:36-42).
findings.why: Once the stub list shows every event, including ones you passed, a Hopper can tap I'M GOING, see it confirmed, and have nothing saved. A fake 'going' undermines the count that the whole list is ordered by.
findings.suggestion: Wire the new button with permissions that already exist. If you previously passed on the event, delete that old swipe, then save 'in'. Tapping 'YOU'RE GOING' again deletes it, which also gives an undo. Show the green stamp only after the save succeeds. If it fails or there's no session, show a short plain error and leave the button orange. No schema change.
findings.gamification_angle: The going count is the scoreboard. It has to be trustworthy for the leaderboard ordering to mean anything.

questions_for_jae: Should 'Any day' exist anywhere in the app? I recommend no: every screen always shows exactly one night, plus the month grid for planning ahead.

Swipe deck: cut it completely, or keep it as an optional 'Can't decide? Swipe tonight' mode behind a link on the Tonight list? The draft lists 'a card in the deck' as a stub, so if it stays, its cards become stubs. Either way, 'I'm going' moves onto the list stubs, because today the deck is the only place to say it.

When someone taps an event on Tonight, should it open the existing event card over the list, or jump to the Map with that event selected? There is no standalone event page yet; the draft's event page would be a separate build.

The design draft contradicts itself. The rule says one tier-2 colour per card, but the sample stub shows a green '14 GOING' pill and a violet 'DROP AT 11' pill together, and the day sample shows blue plus yellow. Which wins on a stub?

What should 'Hoppers going' count: only the 'I'm in' taps (today's swipes_in), or also crew RSVPs marked 'going' (game.ts:42)? Adding RSVPs, or showing other people's faces on a stub, would need a back-end change, because swipes are private today.

On the Map, is a full 14-night rail across the top acceptable, or should it collapse to one 'FRI 9 · 23 ON' chip that opens when tapped? The top row already holds the wordmark, XP chip, filter, bus and crew buttons, and the bottom holds the heat strip, radius slider and area row.
Should the 'N on' counts on the rail follow the 'what kind' filter and the map radius, or always show all of Lagos for that night? I recommend following the type filter but not the radius.
Keep 'This weekend' as a multi-night selection (a bracket over Fri-Sun), or single nights only?
Should unverified lead events appear in the Tonight list at all, or only on the map?
Daytime events (beach, brunch, food): what start time should switch a stub to the cream day look? 5pm?
Conductor line: should 'Hoppers out' mean recent check-ins (the last 3 hours) or people going? I suggest check-ins for tonight and going for future nights.

verify:game-me.surface: Game layer + Me (Me, avatar editor, Quests, Drops rewards, Drop-a-flyer form, Collection, month report card, toasts, badges and levels)
verify:game-me.current_state_summary: Me is one long scrolling page. From the top it shows an avatar header, then a second copy of the avatar in a "Your look" card, then a Hopper-to-Captain card. Below those come the home area, a grid of emoji badges, an orange-tinted Outside Score box, a violet "Found on the map" link, a list of past nights with orange diamonds, a paragraph explaining "the ladder", and account links, including a STAFF link that every user sees. Across Me, Quests, the map header, Crew, the event card and the report card, a user meets about 18 different scores and counters. Those include XP, an XP level, a separate Hop ladder, badges, Outside Score, a points table, Lagos rank, a leaderboard, check-ins, outings, active days, "x/3 days", a daily streak, a week streak, quests, collectibles, drop rewards and "crew moments". Two ladders both end in "Captain", and the Captain card can never get past 1 of 4. Claiming a reward is a single button that drops a "YOU GOT" box into the card. Drops that have not opened yet still show an active claim button, and tapping it says "DROP IS CLOSED". /drops can only be reached from a small REWARDS button on Quests. "Drop" means three things: posting a flyer (/drop), partner rewards (/drops) and collectibles. When one check-in unlocks several badges, only the first one is announced, in a 2.6-second violet toast. The month report card is a small web card behind a copy-link button on Quests, not a 1080x1920 story poster. Body copy is set in an 11px monospace font, and labels go down to 7-9px. Badges, quests and collectibles all use emoji. The design-system mascot, stamp motion and star flight are not used anywhere.

findings.title: Cut about 18 scores down to two number tiles and one rank name
findings.evidence: The Me header packs level name, XP and a check-in count into 9px mono text (src/app/me/page.tsx:92-94). That count can never go above 40, because the query stops at 40 rows (me/page.tsx:45). The Captain card has its own number and bar (me/page.tsx:159-176), and the badge grid is at me/page.tsx:190-218. Outside Score, Lagos rank, outings, 'x/3 days' and the week streak are at me/page.tsx:220-229, with the score at only 24px, text-2xl (me/page.tsx:222). Quests repeats Outside Score at 30px and adds a daily streak, 'x/3 days', a week streak (quests/page.tsx:26), a top-5 board (quests/page.tsx:27), '+N XP' pills (quests/page.tsx:30) and a points table that mentions a 'star level' found nowhere else (quests/page.tsx:38). The map HUD shows level, XP and a bar (src/app/page.tsx:150-160). Crew shows XP and sorts by it (src/app/crew/page.tsx:55,96,168). More XP labels: the event card (src/components/EventCard.tsx:114 'CHECK IN · +50 XP'), event quests (src/components/EventQuestList.tsx:57 '+N XP', :76 'DO THIS · EARN XP'), the quest toast (src/lib/game.ts:15) and the drop result (src/app/drops/page.tsx:19). One check-in is worth +50 XP, or +100 at a Hop stop (supabase/schema.sql:300,328), plus 100 Outside points (schema.sql:1365). The report card adds six more stat tiles (src/app/report/share/[token]/page.tsx:10).
findings.why: The design system says 'Two tiles, not eight'. It lists exactly this sprawl (XP, badges, star level, Outside Score, Lagos rank, four streak types, crew activity) and says two numbers go on the profile and everything else becomes one rank name. Numbers should be 32px+ Poppins Black, and only the one that moved most recently is orange. Today one check-in shows three different rewards, which reads as noise, not a game.
findings.suggestion: On Me, show exactly two big numbers. NIGHTS OUT counts check-ins this month (verified_outings, schema.sql:1463). WEEK STREAK counts weeks in a row with a check-in (outing_streak, schema.sql:1470-1473). Both already arrive through useGameDashboard (src/lib/game.ts:27-29), so no new data is needed. Set them in Poppins Black at 32px+ with a small mono caption, and make orange only the one that changed last. Above them, show one large rank name from the existing ladder (src/lib/brand.ts:31-37) with a thin bar to the next rank, using the progress value the code already works out (brand.ts:49). Remove the XP number and every '+N XP' label: on the map HUD, Crew, the event card button, quest pills, quest and drop toasts, and the drop result. Hide Outside Score, the leaderboard, the daily streak, 'x/3 days' and the points table. Lagos rank appears only once a month, on the report card. Crew can keep its current order behind the scenes and simply show the rank name instead of XP. Nothing changes in the back end: XP still adds up and still decides the rank.
findings.gamification_angle: With fewer numbers, each one matters, and a rank change becomes a rare moment you notice instead of a ticker.

findings.title: Two 'Captain' ladders on one screen, and the Captain card is stuck at 1/4
findings.evidence: The XP ladder runs ROOKIE, HOPPER, NIGHT RUNNER, BRIDGE RAT, CAPTAIN (src/lib/brand.ts:31-37), and its rank shows in the Me header (me/page.tsx:93). A second card also says HOPPER or CAPTAIN, but it is based on Hop badges (me/page.tsx:159-176). Below it, 'The ladder' paragraph says four badges make you Captain (me/page.tsx:258-264). That card counts badge keys equal to 'hop' (me/page.tsx:74). Each badge can only be stored once per person (primary key (user_id,key), supabase/schema.sql:122-127), and awarding it again does nothing (schema.sql:354-355). So progress is always 0 or 1, and the card shows '3 more Hops to make Captain' forever. A user past 1400 XP sees CAPTAIN in the header and HOPPER in the card at the same time. The card's number also sits on a solid violet tile (me/page.tsx:169).
findings.why: Two ranks that contradict each other on one screen, one of which can never move, is a quick way to lose trust in a game. The design system asks for one rank name, 'Rookie to Hopper to Captain, mapping onto the community ladder you already run'.
findings.suggestion: Delete the Captain card and 'The ladder' paragraph. Show a single rank name. Until Jae decides otherwise, use the XP ladder, because it works today and already starts at Rookie/Hopper and ends at Captain. If Captain must mean 'rode four Hops', that is a data decision to settle first (see questions). Its name could replace the XP ladder's middle steps later without any visual change.
findings.gamification_angle: One ladder people can actually climb.

findings.title: Upcoming drops look claimable, then say 'DROP IS CLOSED'
findings.evidence: The drop list keeps any drop that has not closed yet and never checks whether it has opened (src/lib/game.ts:21; the database rule matches, supabase/schema.sql:1192). The card shows a small grey 'opens …' line (drops/page.tsx:18), but the 'CLAIM MYSTERY DROP' button is live regardless (drops/page.tsx:21). Before the opening time, the server answers 'closed' (schema.sql:1288), which the app shows as 'DROP IS CLOSED' (game.ts:23). The event card has the same problem with its 'OPEN DROP' button (EventCard.tsx:144). Opening and closing times are already loaded with every drop (game.ts:7).
findings.why: Being told 'closed' about something that hasn't started breaks trust in the one feature meant to feel scarce and special. The design system's drop screen asks for 'Countdown before, hard cutoff after'.
findings.suggestion: Before a drop opens, show it as sealed. The button reads 'OPENS FRI 22:00' or 'OPENS IN 2H 14M' in DM Mono and cannot be pressed. Once it opens, the button becomes active and a pill shows 'CLOSES 23:30'. After it closes, it leaves the list. This uses only times the app already has. Ship it now, ahead of the full reveal screen below.
findings.gamification_angle: A visible countdown builds anticipation instead of disappointment.

findings.title: Turn claiming a drop into the four-sealed-box reveal
findings.evidence: On /drops, tapping 'CLAIM MYSTERY DROP' puts an inline 'YOU GOT' box in the card and shows a toast (drops/page.tsx:19-21). A second copy with different markup sits on the event card, with a gift emoji and a raw RANDOM/FIXED tag (EventCard.tsx:138-148, 142). On the event card, one code box and one 'YOU GOT' box are shared by every drop (EventCard.tsx:55,57,143,146). There is no share action. The only way into /drops is the REWARDS button on Quests (src/app/quests/page.tsx:25). The map has no violet drop pins. It shows only a 7px '✦ FIND' label on event pins that have a collectible or a live drop (src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:599-601,643-645; src/app/globals.css:221-231; src/lib/useCollectibles.ts:49-63). Drops not attached to an event never appear on the map (useCollectibles.ts:57). The claim already returns the reward name, description, voucher code and XP (game.ts:23; schema.sql:1323). It does not return the badge.
findings.why: The design system calls the drop reveal 'the only extravagance': four sealed boxes, you pick one, tear it with a drag, contents come out face up one at a time and you flick each away. That is 'Four frames: sealed, chosen, torn, pulled', with mascot 'secret before the reveal, win after' and 'one share action producing a stub of what you pulled and where'. Today the product's most valuable moment looks like a form result.
findings.suggestion: Build one full-screen Drop Reveal, opened from the event card and from the drop marker on the map. Upgrade the existing '✦ FIND' label into a proper violet drop pin; the map already knows which events have one. Sealed: four boxes, the countdown or close time in DM Mono, mascot in 'secret'. Chosen: tap a box. The choice changes nothing, exactly as the design system intends. Torn: drag to tear. The existing claim runs here. If it fails ('get closer', 'scan the code'), the box stays sealed and the mascot shows 'oops' with the reason. Pulled: cards turn face up one at a time, first the reward, then the voucher code printed as a ticket serial, then XP if there is any. Flick each away. Mascot 'win', and a star flies into the Me tab. Finish with one button, 'Share', which makes a stub of what you pulled and where. Leave out a badge card, because the claim does not return the badge.
