On the event card, replace the inline claim block with one compact stub per drop: 'LIVE DROP · CLOSES 23:00' plus an OPEN button. Grain and collage are allowed on this screen only. For the box, the lid-pop in Jae's lab (hoppaz-anchor-lab/public/ar.js:261-300, makeGift and burst) is a good reference for shape and motion. Do not copy its colours (#ff4d2e and #ffd23f are off-brand).
findings.gamification_angle: A once-a-night ceremony that brings people back, the lesson the design system takes from Pokemon TCG Pocket.

findings.title: Replace emoji badges and icons with a shelf of stamped stubs
findings.evidence: Badge icons are emoji 🌉🌴🌙🎟🎤🏖📌🚌 (src/lib/brand.ts:53-62), drawn at text-xl, with locked badges faded to 30% grey (me/page.tsx:203). Badges defined on the server default to ✨ (supabase/schema.sql:973). Every badge created from a quest in admin is hard-set to ✨ (src/app/api/admin/game/route.ts:58), and those render as-is (me/page.tsx:217). Collectibles also show emoji (src/app/collection/page.tsx:19; EventCard.tsx:159). Each collectible has an art_url that is loaded but never displayed (src/lib/useCollectibles.ts:6,18,44). Quests use 📸👥▦💡📍 (quests/page.tsx:43) and 📸▦✦ (src/components/EventQuestList.tsx:52). More emoji: 🎁 (EventCard.tsx:142) and ✨ (me/page.tsx:231). How to earn a badge appears only in a hover tooltip (me/page.tsx:197), and the badge tiles cannot be tapped, so on a phone that text never shows.
findings.why: Emoji look different on every phone, are someone else's artwork, and read as a hackathon project. In the design system a badge is a ticket stub that lands like a rubber stamp, and illustration (Tier 4) lives only inside artwork.
findings.suggestion: Turn the badge shelf into a row of ticket stubs with two punched notches. An earned badge gets a one-colour stamp mark (cream at night, ink by day), its name, and the date earned in DM Mono. A locked badge is a dashed outline with its 'how to earn' line printed on it. Tapping any stub opens a small sheet with the details. Commission 8 stamp marks for the 8 built-in badges, plus one generic Hoppaz stamp for quest badges until those get their own art. For quest icons, use the line icons the app already ships (lucide-react, package.json:21), or no icon at all. Show a collectible's art_url when it has one, and fall back to emoji only until art is ready.
findings.gamification_angle: A stamped shelf is the collection people screenshot, and stamps give the 180ms stamp motion a natural place to live.

findings.title: Re-order Me: status first, shelf second, settings last; cut duplicates and internal content
findings.evidence: Current order: avatar header (me/page.tsx:79-106), then a 'Your look' card showing the avatar again over an orange disc (me/page.tsx:141-157), the Captain card (159-176), home area (178-188), badges (190-218), Outside Score (220-229), a violet collection link (230-232), and 'Your nights' with an orange ◆ tile on every row (235-256, 244-246). After that come the ladder paragraph (258-264), a STAFF link shown to everyone (me/page.tsx:269), and delete account in Tailwind red (me/page.tsx:271). REPLAY THE INTRO sits loose at the bottom (274-282). Offline users see a developer note about 'Supabase keys and anonymous sign-ins' (me/page.tsx:284-289). The header avatar already opens the editor (me/page.tsx:81-83). is_admin is part of the profile type (src/lib/types.ts:36), and the full profile row is already loaded (src/lib/useSession.ts:20).
findings.why: The design system's Me screen is 'Two number tiles above the fold, then the badge shelf, then settings', with the rank name as its one moment and a small permanent mascot. Today the useful status sits under three cards of chrome, and some of the content is meant for staff only.
findings.suggestion: New order: (1) avatar (tap to dress), name, the big rank name and the small mascot. (2) The two number tiles. (3) The badge shelf of stubs with 'See all', which also leads to collectibles and claimed rewards. (4) A 'Month report card' row. (5) A collapsed 'Settings' group: name, home area, replay intro, privacy, community rules, and delete account in Fire Ant red. Delete the 'Your look' card. Show STAFF only when is_admin is true. Replace the offline note with 'You're offline. Nothing is saved until you're back.' 'Your nights' is not part of the design system's Me screen. Either move it to Crew's shelf of stubs, or keep it here as one sideways row of punched stubs (event, area, date in mono) instead of a list with orange diamonds.
findings.gamification_angle: Status on top, collection in the middle, admin at the bottom: the tab exists to show progress.

findings.title: Add the small permanent mascot to Me, driven by data the page already loads
findings.evidence: There is no mascot anywhere in the app (no matches for 'mascot' in src/). The rig already defines the states idle, wave, welcome, oya, secret, point, celebrate, win, oops and sleep, switched by a data-state attribute (Hoppaz-Mascot-Rig.html:80-96), plus a tap squash (Hoppaz-Mascot-Rig.html:208-210). Me already loads past check-ins, newest first (me/page.tsx:40-45), so the date of the last night out is known. It also has outing_streak and active_days_this_week from the game stats (src/lib/game.ts:29).
findings.why: The design system's one exception is a small permanent mascot in Me that reflects real status: 'asleep after two weeks indoors, celebrating on a live streak'. It is a status readout disguised as a character and gives the tab a reason to be opened.
findings.suggestion: Place a small mascot next to the rank name, with the default ground edge. It sleeps if the last night out was more than 14 days ago, celebrates if you have been out this week and your week streak is 2 or more, and idles otherwise. It waves on the first open of the day (remembered on the phone only) and squashes when tapped. Also use it in these empty states: no nights yet (me/page.tsx:236-238), empty collection (collection/page.tsx:18), no live drops (drops/page.tsx:16), and the report card's missing not-found state. Keep it off every list and scrolling feed.
findings.gamification_angle: It feels alive without adding another number.

findings.title: Remove the Quests page and keep quests compact on the event card
findings.evidence: Quests repeats Me's score card (quests/page.tsx:26 vs me/page.tsx:220-229). It adds a leaderboard (quests/page.tsx:27), raw labels such as 'WEEKLY · CHECKIN' (quests/page.tsx:30) and a points table (quests/page.tsx:38). It also has a 'Choose an event' dropdown listing every event within 45 km (quests/page.tsx:14,33; useEvents takes a radius in km, src/lib/useEvents.ts:19). Every quest not tied to an event already appears on every event card, and event quests appear on their own event (EventQuestList.tsx:18). On the card they show as an orange-tinted panel full of inputs, textareas and dropdowns (EventQuestList.tsx:33,64-74). The only way into Quests is 'DETAILS →' on Me (me/page.tsx:227). The report card button lives only here (quests/page.tsx:26), and so does the only link to /drops (quests/page.tsx:25).
findings.why: It is a second dashboard of the numbers the design system removes, and it is form-heavy in the middle of the game. The design system has no Quests screen. Jae also wants the event tap decluttered, so whatever stays on the event card has to be small.
findings.suggestion: Remove the Quests page from the app. On the event card, show quests as one line each: title, plus the badge stub it unlocks, using quest.badge_key (game.ts:6). The badge's name is already the quest title (admin/game/route.ts:58). Otherwise show nothing. The code box, text box or crew picker opens only when you tap a quest, and quests that need a check-in stay folded until you have checked in. Move 'Make last month's report card' to Me. Because /drops loses its only entry point, add a 'Live drops' row on Me or in Tonight's conductor line ('Two drops tonight'). Drops with no event (area or partner drops) appear on no event card or map pin, so they would otherwise be unreachable.
findings.gamification_angle: Quests become things to do at the party, not homework on a separate page.

findings.title: Let 'Drop' mean only the reward: rename the flyer flow
findings.evidence: The map's + button opens /drop, labelled 'Drop a flyer on the map' (src/app/page.tsx:296-298) and titled 'Drop a flyer' (src/app/drop/page.tsx:105). Its button reads 'DROP IT ON THE MAP' / 'DROPPING…' (drop/page.tsx:193), its toast reads 'DROPPED · WAITING ON AN ADMIN' in violet (drop/page.tsx:98), and its badge is 'Flyer drop' (brand.ts:60; drop/page.tsx:196-197). Meanwhile /drops is 'Live drops' rewards (drops/page.tsx:15), the event card says 'LIVE DROP · REAL REWARD' (EventCard.tsx:140), and the button says 'CLAIM MYSTERY DROP' (drops/page.tsx:21). The two web addresses differ by one letter.
findings.why: In the design system, 'Drop' is the violet, scarce, once-a-night reward. Using the same word for 'submit an event' weakens the reward and confuses new users.
findings.suggestion: Change the words only. The flyer flow becomes 'Post a flyer' (header), 'PUT IT ON THE MAP' (button) and 'SENT · AN ADMIN CHECKS IT FIRST' (a plain toast, not violet). The badge becomes 'Plug' or 'Flyer poster'. Engineers can keep the /drop address or move it to /add. Use the word 'drop' only for partner rewards and their reveal.
findings.gamification_angle: Keeps 'drop' special, so a drop always means something rare.

findings.title: A check-in can unlock several badges, but only the first is shown
findings.evidence: One check-in can award several badges at once: mainland or island, After 11, No gate fee, Comedy, Beach and On the bus (supabase/schema.sql:331-339). The server returns every newly earned badge (schema.sql:343-346). The app reads only the first (src/lib/useCheckin.ts:66). Badges that are not in the built-in list show their raw key in capitals (useCheckin.ts:68-69).
findings.why: Badges are one of only three moments the design system allows star flight for. A first night out at a free, late island party earns three badges but shows one 2.6-second toast, so two moments are lost.
findings.suggestion: After a check-in, play one stamp per new badge, in a row: each stub stamps in for 180ms, slightly off square. The mascot celebrates once, and one star per badge flies into the Me tab. Names come from the built-in list, or the badge catalogue for quest badges. The data is already in the check-in result, so this is display only.
findings.gamification_angle: A triple-stamp first night is the hook that makes a new user come back.

findings.title: Toasts and motion: stamp badges, fly stars, stop announcing every XP
findings.evidence: Every check-in toast announces the XP: 'CHECKED IN · +50 XP', or +100 at a Hop stop (src/lib/useCheckin.ts:71). A badge unlock is just a violet toast (useCheckin.ts:66-69). It fades up (src/components/Toaster.tsx:14; tailwind.config.ts:32,37) and disappears after 2.6s (src/lib/store.ts:73). The toast is a solid violet slab (Toaster.tsx:17). Violet is also used for 'QR CODE READ' (drops/page.tsx:24; EventQuestList.tsx:80; EventCard.tsx:147), the flyer toast (drop/page.tsx:98), 'REPORT LINK COPIED' (quests/page.tsx:26), quest completion (EventQuestList.tsx:29) and 'ADDED TO YOUR COLLECTION' (EventCard.tsx:161). Errors such as 'TOO FAR' get the same cream style as successes, because the default tone renders cream (useCheckin.ts:56; Toaster.tsx:17; store.ts:64-66). The avatar re-animates on every tap in the editor (src/app/me/avatar/page.tsx:75).
findings.why: The design system asks for 'Stamp, not bounce' (180ms, hard ease-out), and star flight 'on badges, rank changes and drops only', never for each individual XP. Violet means scarcity only, and Tier-2 colours never fill a surface. Today the biggest moment, a badge, gets the same slip as 'QR read'.
findings.suggestion: Badge unlock: see the multi-badge stamp above. Rank change: the rank name stamps in on Me the next time it opens. Drops: star flight at the end of the reveal. The star-flight code already exists in the rig (Hoppaz-Mascot-Rig.html:509-545); the stamp has to be built. A plain check-in gets a quiet 'CHECKED IN' with no number. Restyle toasts as a dark card with cream text and one coloured dot: green (Keke) for success, red (Fire Ant) for errors, violet only for drops. This needs a third tone in the app's toast helper (store.ts:64-66), which is display-only. Toasts appear instantly, with no fade-up. In the avatar editor, drop the re-pop or replace it with a single 180ms stamp.
findings.gamification_angle: Restraint everywhere else is what makes the stamp and the star flight land.

findings.title: Body text is in tiny mono; fonts don't match the design system
findings.evidence: The app loads only Poppins 400/600/900 and Space Mono (src/app/layout.tsx:4-8; globals.css:9). There is no Archivo and no DM Mono. Body text defaults to Poppins at weight 400 (globals.css:16). All explanatory copy uses the 'hint' style, which is mono at 11px (globals.css:66-68), and that is most of the text on Me, Quests, Drops and Collection. Section labels are 9px (globals.css:63-65) and pills are 8.5px (globals.css:50-53). Badge names are 8px (me/page.tsx:208), quest details are 8px (quests/page.tsx:30), bottom-nav labels are 8px (src/components/BottomNav.tsx:41), and the map's FIND label is 7px (globals.css:226).
findings.why: The design system sets Archivo 400/500/600 for 'everything you read', DM Mono only for labels, dates, prices and serials, and Poppins never below 600. Paragraphs in 11px monospace and 8px labels are the clearest sign of an unfinished product on a cheap Android screen.
findings.suggestion: Load Archivo and set every descriptive line (all 'hint' text) in Archivo at about 13px. Swap Space Mono for DM Mono and use it only for labels, dates, prices and voucher codes, never below 10px. Keep Poppins for headlines, rank names, buttons and numbers at 600 or 900 only. This is a font and size change; no layout logic moves.
findings.gamification_angle: Plain, readable working text is what lets the loud moments (stamps, reveal, report card) look intentional.

findings.title: Make the month report card a 1080x1920 story poster
findings.evidence: The share page is a small max-w-md web card (src/app/report/share/[token]/page.tsx:10), not a 9:16 poster. Its header is a solid orange block. It shows six equal stat tiles, four with the same Sparkles icon (report/share/[token]/page.tsx:10-11), including Outside Score, quests and 'crew moments'. There is no mascot and no collage, and the image cannot be saved. The only way to create it is a ghost button on Quests that copies a link (quests/page.tsx:26). A bad or expired link shows 'LOADING REPORT…' forever, because nothing handles an empty result (report/share/[token]/page.tsx:10). The saved Lagos rank can be empty (supabase/schema.sql:1574), which renders an empty tile. The saved snapshot already holds verified_outings and outing_streak (schema.sql:1569 plus 1474).
findings.why: The design system calls this 'the organic growth engine': loud layer, a portrait poster that drops straight into a story, nights out, one superlative, and the mascot celebrating with an ink edge in full sticker treatment.
findings.suggestion: Design it as a poster that happens to be generated. Tilted Poppins Black reads 'TEMI WAS OUTSIDE.', with the month in DM Mono, one hero number (nights out) and the week streak. Add one superlative line from Lagos rank ('#12 IN LAGOS THIS MONTH'), shown only when there is a rank. Use the mascot celebrating with an ink edge, plus grain and collage. Two buttons: 'Save to story' (renders the poster as a 1080x1920 image on the phone) and 'Send on WhatsApp'. Put the trigger on Me from the 1st of the month. Add a not-found state with the mascot in 'oops'. 'Where you went and who with' is not in the saved snapshot, so adding it needs a small data change (see questions).
findings.gamification_angle: Every shared poster is an ad for going out with Hoppaz.

findings.title: Stop tinting game cards and using orange as decoration
findings.evidence: Tinted surfaces: the Outside Score box at bg-orange/10 (me/page.tsx:220), the collection link at bg-violet/10 (me/page.tsx:230), the drop card's violet border and violet icon well (drops/page.tsx:17-18), the event card's drop and collectible panels at bg-violet/10 (EventCard.tsx:139,152), the quest panel at bg-orange/5 (EventQuestList.tsx:33), quest icon wells (quests/page.tsx:30; EventQuestList.tsx:51), and collectible tiles at bg-violet/10 (collection/page.tsx:19). Orange on things you can't tap: earned-badge borders (me/page.tsx:200), the Captain bar (me/page.tsx:174), the ◆ tile on every past night (me/page.tsx:244), the LAGOS and '+XP' pills (me/page.tsx:223; quests/page.tsx:30; EventQuestList.tsx:57), event names in Collection (collection/page.tsx:19-20), 'YOU GOT' labels (drops/page.tsx:19; EventCard.tsx:146), and the report header (report/share/[token]/page.tsx:10). The avatar ring (me/page.tsx:84) and the disc in 'Your look' (me/page.tsx:152) are inside links, so they are technically tappable, but they read as wallpaper. Violet is used for non-scarce things: the Captain number (me/page.tsx:169) and the flyer info note (drop/page.tsx:109). Colour values drift from the design system: dim #8A7C73, ink-2 #17110F, ink-3 #231915 and line #2E211C (brand.ts:2-12; tailwind.config.ts:12-17), where the design system has #9C9087, #171210, #221A17 and #2E2320. Hard-coded #A98CFF and #A89588 appear at drops/page.tsx:18, me/page.tsx:285, drop/page.tsx:109 and globals.css:58, and Tailwind red is used for delete (me/page.tsx:271). The only state colour defined is an off-spec green 'ok' #49D07A (tailwind.config.ts:18). There is no Lagoon, Danfo or Fire Ant. The 'Never a fifth colour' comment (brand.ts:1; tailwind.config.ts:4) is now superseded by the design system's Tier 2.
findings.why: The design system's rules: orange is a verb (if it is orange you can tap it), Tier-2 colours never paint a surface, at most one Tier-2 colour per card, and violet means live drop or rare only.
findings.suggestion: Put every game card on the plain night-card ground with a thin hairline and at most one coloured pill: violet 'LIVE DROP', green 'CLAIMED' or yellow 'CLOSING SOON'. Remove orange from badge borders, diamonds, the score box, the +XP and LAGOS pills, collection labels and the report header, and drop the solid orange behind the header avatar. Align the colour values with the design system, replace 'ok' with Keke, and add Lagoon, Danfo and Fire Ant with their day twins, so nobody has to hard-code hex values again.
findings.gamification_angle: When violet only ever means 'drop', a violet pill on the map makes people move.

findings.title: Turn Collection into one shelf of stubs and show the real art
findings.evidence: Collection holds two unrelated lists. One is emoji collectibles in a 2-column grid of violet-tinted tiles (collection/page.tsx:19). The other is drop rewards, where the voucher code sits in a selectable mono box with no copy button and the date is in small grey text (collection/page.tsx:20). art_url is fetched but never shown (useCollectibles.ts:44). There are two ways in: a violet ✨ card on Me (me/page.tsx:230-231) and 'COLLECTION →' on the event card (EventCard.tsx:155).
findings.why: In the design system, a claimed drop is a ticket stub. A reward you have to show at a gate must be easy to find and copy in one tap.
findings.suggestion: Call it 'Your shelf'. Every collectible and claimed reward becomes a punched stub: name in Poppins Black, partner and date in DM Mono. Print voucher codes as a ticket serial with a COPY lip button. Use art_url when it exists, and the mascot for the empty state. Reach it from 'See all' on the Me badge shelf instead of a separate violet card.
findings.gamification_angle: A shelf of stubs that feels physical keeps people coming back, and the design system prefers it to scores.

findings.title: Drop card copy: fix the swapped labels, remove internal terms, add 'closes' and 'left' pills
findings.evidence: The /drops card labels are swapped. A 'random' drop is described as 'sponsor-selected reward pool' and a 'fixed' one as 'surprise reward' (drops/page.tsx:18). The event card always says 'surprise reward' and then shows the raw RANDOM or FIXED value as a pill (EventCard.tsx:142). The close time is never shown (drops/page.tsx:18). The drop query does not ask for max_claims or claimed_count (game.ts:21), but both columns exist (supabase/schema.sql:1061-1062), the app is allowed to read the table (schema.sql:1547), and the admin screen already reads them (src/app/api/admin/game/route.ts:22).
findings.why: Admin terms are leaking to users, and here they are wrong. The design system uses mono pills for state, and yellow (Danfo) for 'last tickets, nearly gone'.
findings.suggestion: Each drop card shows the title and partner, plus one pill at most: 'CLOSES 23:00' (yellow in the last hour), or 'SCAN QR AT THE BAR' when a code is needed. Remove the random/fixed wording entirely. A yellow '12 LEFT' pill only needs those two existing columns added to the app's drop query. That is a tiny hookup, with no database change.
findings.gamification_angle: Visible scarcity ('12 left') is the strongest nudge there is, and it costs almost nothing.

findings.title: Flyer form: replace the native date picker with the night rail
findings.evidence: The form uses the phone's built-in date and time pickers (drop/page.tsx:162,169). The default date comes from new Date().toISOString() (drop/page.tsx:22), which is UTC time, so between midnight and 1am in Lagos it defaults to yesterday. The app already formats Lagos dates correctly elsewhere (game.ts:13). There is a violet-bordered info note in hard-coded grey (drop/page.tsx:109). No night rail exists in the app yet. Tonight and the map filter also use the built-in date picker (src/app/discover/page.tsx:101; src/components/FilterCard.tsx:72).
findings.why: Jae wants date selection on brand everywhere. The design system's date control is a 14-night rail (weekday, date) with the month grid hidden behind a calendar icon, because 'Nobody going out picks October 17, they pick Friday.'
findings.suggestion: Build the night rail once and use it in Tonight, the map filter and this form. That means 14 chips (THU 08, FRI 09…), a calendar icon for later dates, and time chips (6PM, 8PM, 9PM, 10PM, 11PM, LATE, OTHER). The caption reader keeps pre-filling them. Default to today in Lagos time. Restyle the info note as a plain hairline, or blue (Lagoon, the 'information' colour).

findings.title: Keep the avatar editor; just calm it down
findings.evidence: It has six tabs and a wardrobe of Lagos labels (src/app/me/avatar/page.tsx:16-23,157-184). An orange 'sun' sits behind the figure; the code comments describe it as from the Rough Cut style (avatar/page.tsx:73-74). The figure re-animates on every change (avatar/page.tsx:75), and the selected tab is solid orange (avatar/page.tsx:90).
findings.why: Dressing a Hopper in Lagos labels is on-brand and gamified, and it is the user's own identity on the map. The only conflicts are motion (it moves on every tap) and the risk of the orange backdrop spreading beyond this screen.
findings.suggestion: Keep it, with two touches. Remove the re-pop on every tap, or make it a single 180ms stamp. Treat the orange sun as artwork (Tier 4, Rough Cut), which is allowed on this creative screen but should not be copied onto Me. The selected tab can stay orange because tabs are tappable.
findings.gamification_angle: Identity is a reward in itself, so don't bury it under scores.

questions_for_jae: The two tiles: the data tracks 'weeks in a row with a night out' (outing_streak), not weekends specifically, while the design system tile says WEEKEND STREAK. Is labelling it WEEK STREAK OK? A true weekend streak needs a small back-end change. (The app does count weekend check-ins this week, but not as a streak.)

Which ladder survives? The design system says the rank should map 'onto the community ladder you already run' (Hopper to Captain via Hop rides), but that Hop ladder is broken in the app today. The XP ladder (Rookie, Hopper, Night Runner, Bridge Rat, Captain) works. Use the XP ladder for now, or fix how Hops are counted first?

Outside Score and the Lagos leaderboard: OK to hide both from the everyday app and keep Lagos rank only as the superlative on the month report card? Or do partners or Ola's team rely on the leaderboard?
On Me: is the mascot a separate small character next to the user's dressed Hopper, or should the user's own avatar take on the mascot's moods (asleep, celebrating)?
OK to rename the flyer flow to 'Post a flyer' so 'Drop' means only the reward ceremony? And rename the 'Flyer drop' badge?
Who draws the 8 badge stamp marks, the generic quest-badge stamp and the collectible art: the brand designer, or should we derive them from the mascot rig's line style?

Report card: should 'where you went and who with' be on the poster? It is not in the saved monthly snapshot today, so it would need a small data addition. And should the card appear automatically on the 1st, or stay a button?
Quests: retire the Quests page completely (quests live only on event cards), or keep a small 'This week' list on Me?

Partner drops that are not tied to an event currently appear on no map pin and no event card. Where should they show up: a 'Live drops' row on Me, Tonight's conductor line, or their own violet pin on the map?

verify:social.surface: Crew + Chat + Avatars (src/app/crew, src/app/chat, src/app/chat/dm/[id], src/components/chat/*, src/components/Avatar.tsx, src/lib/avatar*.ts, src/lib/chat.ts, src/lib/useCrew.ts, src/lib/game.ts useGroups, src/app/community)
verify:social.current_state_summary: The Crew tab is one long scroll. It has a "Your crews" box (create a crew, pick Private/Open, join by code, each crew with its raw invite code and every planned move, plus up to 50 strangers' open crews), then a name search, then a separate one-way friends list that is also called "crew", then an XP leaderboard. Those friends are also drawn as faces on the map, but at a made-up spot near the centre of their home area, while the copy promises "who is out and where they are". Planned moves show past and future together with the oldest first, and the I'M IN / MAYBE / CAN'T GO buttons save without changing anything on screen. Chat uses two orange lip buttons as a tab switch and a row of up to 8 event rooms picked by heat from the next 45 days. Its feed has orange author names, brown bubbles that aren't brand colours, body text in Poppins 400, no timestamps and no auto-scroll. Waves, DMs, block, report and mutual name reveal all work, but block and report behave differently in the person sheet and in a DM, and the inbox count never goes down. Faces are a Bitmoji-style avatar on orange (named) or violet (anonymous) filled circles, and a person who never dressed up looks three different ways across Crew, Chat and the map. The app only loads Poppins and Space Mono and only has night colours, so the draft's Archivo, DM Mono, state colours and day ground don't exist yet.

findings.title: Take crew faces (and your own avatar) off the map
findings.evidence: src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:749-777 draws a face marker for every friend plus 'me'. faceMarker (NightMap.tsx:68-81) can't be tapped: it is pointer-events-none (line 70) and sits on a filled orange disc (line 72). 'Me' also gets an orange ring (line 769). Friend positions are made up: src/lib/useCrew.ts:10-19 pins each friend at the centre of their profile's home area plus a hash offset (lines 16-17). Your own pin is a guess too when you picked an area instead of sharing GPS (src/lib/store.ts:8,11; src/components/AreaPicker.tsx:63). The toggle is at src/app/page.tsx:187-199 and feeds NightMap at page.tsx:127. Three lines of copy promise live location: src/app/crew/page.tsx:62 ('Who is out and where they are'), crew/page.tsx:121-123 ('their pins show up where they are') and src/app/me/page.tsx:145 ('Your crew sees it on the map').
findings.why: The draft gives the map to content: events, orange heat, and violet pins for drops only. Jae wants map 'models' only where events are. Friends' faces at made-up spots read as live tracking, which becomes a trust problem the first time someone says 'I'm not in Lekki'. Orange on a pin you can't tap breaks Tier 1 ('nothing orange is ever inert').
findings.suggestion: Remove the crew button from the top of the map and stop drawing friends' faces. Replace your own avatar pin with a plain 'you are here' dot: small, cream, dark edge, no face, no orange. Only show the dot when the phone actually shared GPS. If you only picked an area, show no dot. Delete the three lines of copy that promise faces on the map. Show crew presence only where it's true: on a crew's next-move stub, and on an event stub when one of your crews has planned a move to that event ('YOUR CREW · 3 IN'). Showing 'friends going' on every event isn't possible without back-end work, because check-ins and swipes are private to each person (supabase/schema.sql:430, 434). Crew moves and their RSVPs, however, are readable by crew members (schema.sql:1435-1437).
findings.gamification_angle: Crew presence becomes a reason to open an event or a crew plan, instead of decoration on the map.

findings.title: Show who's in, and make 'I'M IN' visibly do something
findings.evidence: src/app/crew/page.tsx:181 renders I'M IN / MAYBE / CAN'T GO as three tags, each calling `void onRsvp(...)`. The true/false result is thrown away, so there is no toast and no selected state. The save is useGroups' rsvp in src/lib/game.ts:42: it upserts and never reloads. RSVPs are never read back anywhere in src/ (game.ts:42 is the only reference). The table and the member-read policy already exist (supabase/schema.sql:1145-1151; policy at 1437). crew_move_rsvps.user_id references profiles (schema.sql:1147), and profiles are publicly readable (schema.sql:408), so names and faces can be joined in.
findings.why: 'Who has RSVP'd' is one of the three things the draft says Crew must show. A button with no feedback reads as broken, and that's the least professional thing on this surface.
findings.suggestion: Replace the three tags with one segmented pill control (mono caps, 1px border, transparent). The chosen option stays visibly selected: Keke green border for IN, dim for MAYBE, dim and struck-through for CAN'T GO. Under the next move, show a row of faces for IN and a smaller dim row for MAYBE, with a mono count ('4 IN · 1 MAYBE'). Small data hookup: the crews loader (useGroups, src/lib/game.ts:37) needs one more read of crew_move_rsvps, joined to each person's name and look. It should re-run after a tap. No schema change.
findings.gamification_angle: Tapping I'M IN stamps your face into the IN row with the 180ms rubber-stamp motion, the same as 'I'm going' on the event page. Seeing friends' faces fill the row pulls in the people who haven't answered yet.

findings.title: Rebuild Crew around 'next move' plus a shelf of punched stubs
findings.evidence: src/app/crew/page.tsx:59-172 stacks these sections in order: header (60-63); a crews box holding create, Private/Open, join by code, your crews, and up to 50 strangers' open crews (65-71); name search (73-118); friends list (120-152); XP leaderboard (154-172). Moves load oldest first with no date filter (src/lib/game.ts:37 `.order("starts_at")`), so every past move sits ABOVE the next one and still shows RSVP buttons (crew/page.tsx:181). A move linked to an event saves event_id (crew/page.tsx:180), but the move row never shows which event it is (line 181). Crew members are never shown: only your own membership row is read (game.ts:37 `.eq("user_id",userId)`).
findings.why: The draft defines Crew as 'small persistent named groups, the next planned move, who has RSVP'd, and the shared history as a shelf of stubs'. Its one gamified moment is the shelf: 'a shared memory rather than a number'. Today the page is a settings form with a leaderboard attached, and old plans bury the next one.
findings.suggestion: Make each crew one block. At the top: the crew name in Poppins Black, with a small row of member faces. Then the NEXT MOVE as a big ticket stub with two punched notches, showing the title, mono date and time, meeting spot, the linked event's name if there is one, and the RSVP control. Below that is THE SHELF: a horizontal row of small punched stubs, one per past move (title and mono date), newest first, with no RSVP buttons. Splitting past from next by start time, and naming the linked event from the events list the page already loads (crew/page.tsx:21), needs no new data. Member faces need one extra read of crew_members joined to profiles, which members can already read (schema.sql:1433, 408). If someone has several crews, show a short list of crew names that each open their crew.
findings.gamification_angle: The shelf fills up with nights you actually did together, which is the retention hook the draft names. A thin shelf nudges people to plan the next one.

findings.title: Load the draft's fonts and colours before restyling Crew and Chat
findings.evidence: src/app/layout.tsx:4-8 loads only Poppins (400/600/900) and Space Mono. Archivo and DM Mono are not loaded. src/app/globals.css:16 makes Poppins the default body font. So room messages (src/app/chat/page.tsx:71: font-display with no weight, so 400) and DM bubbles (src/app/chat/dm/[id]/page.tsx:31, inherited) are Poppins 400 at 13.5px. tailwind.config.ts:12-19 holds only night colours, and they don't match the draft: ink-2 #17110F (draft Night raised #171210), ink-3 #231915 (Night card #221A17), dim #8A7C73 (Night dim #9C9087), line #2E211C (hairline #2E2320), ok #49D07A (Keke #2FD35C). There are no Lagoon, Danfo or Fire Ant colours, and no day ground (globals.css:7 `color-scheme: dark`; body bg-ink at :16).
findings.why: Per the draft, Archivo is 'everything you read', Poppins is 'never below 600', DM Mono is for labels, dates and prices, there is a fixed set of five state colours, and the theme follows the Lagos clock. Every restyle proposed on this surface needs these to exist first: Archivo bubbles, Keke 'IN', Fire Ant 'Block', and day/night grounds.
findings.suggestion: Before touching Crew or Chat, set up the draft's building blocks once for the whole app. Add Archivo and DM Mono, self-hosted like the current fonts (a small front-end package, nothing on the back end), and make Archivo the default reading font. Replace the colour list with the draft's night set, day set and the five state colours. Crew and Chat then show a cream ground in Lagos daytime and black after dark. Every other surface shares this work, so do it once, not per screen.

findings.title: Chat rooms: show tonight only, always name the room you are in, say when it closes
findings.evidence: src/app/chat/page.tsx:35 builds rooms from BASE plus `events.slice(0, 8)`. Those events cover the next 45 days and are sorted by heat (src/lib/useEvents.ts:41, 52), so rooms appear for parties weeks away, as all-caps mono pills (chat/page.tsx:35, 58). Event cards and the Hop sheet deep-link into rooms (src/components/EventCard.tsx:116 and 238; src/components/HopSheet.tsx:78 uses `hop-<id>`). If that room isn't in the top 8, no pill lights up (chat/page.tsx:58), and nothing on screen names the room (line 61 only shows LIVE/ROOM CHAT plus your name). The bus room never gets a name. The server already hides event rooms 24 hours after the event ends (supabase/schema.sql:641-651), but the UI never says so.
findings.why: The draft says 'event rooms that close when the event does'. A room list full of far-off events, and a room you land in with no title, look unfinished.
findings.suggestion: List BASE plus rooms for events happening tonight or live now, using the start times the app already has. Put a plain title line above the feed: the event name in Poppins, then a mono caption ('ROOM CLOSES TOMORROW', 'THE HOP · BUS ROOM', or 'BASE · ALWAYS OPEN'). Any room you deep-linked into always shows as the first, selected pill. Rooms for future nights are not listed. On those events' cards, the chat button can read 'ROOM OPENS ON THE NIGHT'.
findings.gamification_angle: A room that only exists on the night is a small 'you had to be there' scarcity, and going out becomes the way in.

findings.title: Friends you add can silently disappear from the list
findings.evidence: src/lib/useCrew.ts:10-12 returns null for anyone whose area is empty or not in the app's area list, and useCrew.ts:50-51 drops those people. After the 'X ADDED' toast (src/app/crew/page.tsx:103), that person never appears in the friends list. The 'somewhere in Lagos' fallback at crew/page.tsx:137 can never show. Search only hides people already in the filtered list (crew/page.tsx:89), so they keep showing an add button. A second tap then fails on the existing row (supabase/schema.sql:161 primary key) with 'COULD NOT ADD'.
findings.why: 'I added Tunde and he isn't there' is a visible bug, and it undercuts trust in the whole social layer.
findings.suggestion: Show everyone you added, whether or not they set an area. People with no area just have no area line. The filter only exists to place faces on the map, so it can go once map faces go (first finding). It's a one-line front-end change at src/lib/useCrew.ts:50-51 with no back-end change. If the friends list is retired (see 'Untangle'), this bug goes with it.

findings.title: 'Plan a move' should use the night rail, not a browser date picker
findings.evidence: src/app/crew/page.tsx:180 is a raw form. It uses a native `type="datetime-local"` input, and a `<select>` of every loaded event title (45 days, heat order, no dates; useEvents.ts:41, 52) under the option 'General crew move'. The button reads 'SAVE THE MOVE'. The app has no night rail yet: Tonight and the map filter also use native date inputs (src/app/discover/page.tsx:101; src/components/FilterCard.tsx:72).
findings.why: Jae wants date selection to be on brand. The draft's answer is the night rail: 14 nights showing weekday, date and 'N on', because 'nobody going out picks October 17, they pick Friday'. A native date-time picker and an undated 45-day dropdown are the least on-brand controls in the app.
findings.suggestion: Build the night rail once and use it here and in Tonight. 'Plan a move' becomes a bottom sheet in three steps. 1) Pick a night on the rail. 2) Pick one of that night's events (shown as small stubs), which fills in the title and time from the event, or pick 'Our own thing' and type a title. 3) Adjust the time with mono chips (8PM, 9PM, 10PM, 11PM, MIDNIGHT, OTHER), add an optional meeting spot and note, then press PLAN IT (orange lip). The saved fields are exactly the same as today: title, meetup, starts_at, event_id, note.
findings.gamification_angle: The plan appears straight away as the crew's NEXT MOVE stub, which starts the RSVP loop.

findings.title: Make Chat deliberately plain
findings.evidence: src/app/chat/page.tsx:52-53 uses two full orange lip buttons as a tab switch. The selected room pill is filled solid orange (line 58). Line 61 shows a green 'LIVE' that only means the realtime socket connected, in `text-ok` #49D07A, which is not Keke (tailwind.config.ts:18). Line 71 has: author names in orange mono, brown bubble colours that aren't in the palette (#4A2D1E/#2A1A12, also used at dm/[id]/page.tsx:31), and message text in Poppins 400 at 13.5px. There are no timestamps, although created_at is already fetched (src/lib/chat.ts:13). The room feed never scrolls to new messages (no scroll ref at chat/page.tsx:65), while the DM feed does (dm/[id]/page.tsx:18-19). The anonymous switch is a native checkbox (chat/page.tsx:76).
findings.why: The draft says Chat is 'deliberately plain' and its moment is 'None. That is the decision.' Orange should only mean 'tap this'. Reading text should be Archivo, and Poppins should never go below weight 600. State colours are for real states, not 'socket connected'. WhatsApp is the benchmark, and it never hides new messages below the fold.
findings.suggestion: Replace the two orange buttons with a quiet two-tab underline: cream text with an orange underline on the active tab, dim text otherwise. Do the same for room pills: the selected room gets a cream border and cream text, not an orange fill. Remove the LIVE line, and only show a dim 'RECONNECTING…' when the connection drops. Author names become dim mono caps. Bubbles use the ground colours: theirs on Night card #221A17, yours on Night raised #171210 with a hairline edge, and the day versions in daytime. Message text uses Archivo 400 at 14-15px (needs the font finding). Put a tiny mono time under each message ('23:41'), and scroll to the newest message when one arrives. Replace the checkbox with a small pill in the composer showing who you're posting as ('AS YOU' / 'AS SUYA RIDER 4F'), which flips when tapped.

findings.title: Stop painting orange and violet behind faces and on toasts
findings.evidence: Faces sit on filled orange discs: src/components/chat/ChatFace.tsx:28 (`border-orange bg-orange`), src/app/crew/page.tsx:201, src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:72, src/app/me/page.tsx:84 and :152. Anonymous faces sit on filled violet (ChatFace.tsx:28). Faces with no avatar are an orange letter square in search results and for 'you' on the leaderboard, and a cream square for friends (crew/page.tsx:189-192). Wave chips are violet-bordered with an off-palette #A98CFF text (chat/page.tsx:64; src/app/globals.css:57-59). Violet toasts paint a full violet surface (src/components/Toaster.tsx:17) and are used for successes (crew/page.tsx:67-70; chat/page.tsx:64; PersonCard.tsx:34; dm/[id]/page.tsx:30). The 'orange' tone actually renders as a plain cream box (Toaster.tsx:17; default tone at src/lib/store.ts:71). So errors like 'CODE NOT FOUND' look identical to chat's best moment, 'YOU BOTH WAVED. SAY HI' (src/lib/chat.ts:118, shown with 'orange' at chat/page.tsx:64). All toasts are Poppins Black caps (Toaster.tsx:15).
findings.why: Tier 1: nothing orange is ever inert, and a face isn't a button. Tier 2: violet means live drop, rare or scarce only, and state colours never paint a surface. These rules break on almost every row of Crew and Chat, which is why the screens look busy rather than premium. Right now a toast can't tell you whether something worked.
findings.suggestion: Faces sit on a neutral circle (Night card #221A17) with a 1px hairline ring. Anonymous people get a dashed hairline ring and a mono 'ANON' caption, not a violet fill. Toasts become a neutral raised card with Archivo text in normal sentence case: a Keke-green dot for success, Fire Ant red text for errors. 'You both waved' gets the success treatment. Wave chips (if kept; see 'WHO'S HERE') are plain text with a hairline border, with orange only on the action word.
findings.gamification_angle: Holding violet back means it lands harder when a real drop appears.

findings.title: The inbox count never goes down
findings.evidence: src/app/chat/page.tsx:53 shows `waves.length + dms.length` on the tab. my_waves returns only pending waves (supabase/schema.sql:839), but my_dms returns every chat you've ever opened (schema.sql:855-880), and there is no 'unread' field (src/lib/types.ts:79-91). Someone with five old chats sees '· 5' forever. Inbox rows show no time either, although last_at is already fetched (types.ts:90) and is unused at chat/page.tsx:82.
findings.why: A number that looks like 'unread' but never clears teaches people to ignore it, so real waves get missed. That is the opposite of a clean, gamified signal.
findings.suggestion: Count only waves waiting for an answer, which is exact. Show that number in a small orange dot on the tab. On each chat row, add a mono time on the right ('23:41', 'FRI') using the time already fetched. Don't suggest unread messages until there is an unread signal.
findings.gamification_angle: A pending wave is the one social 'someone noticed you' moment in Chat, so the dot should mean exactly that.

findings.title: Fix the person sheet and DM safety controls
findings.evidence: src/components/chat/PersonCard.tsx:82-92 gives WAVE, BLOCK and REPORT equal weight in a 3-column grid. Line 41 uses the browser's window.confirm() for Block. Line 64 slides up with a generic `animate-rise`. The sheet has no Escape-key, focus or aria-modal handling (lines 60-66), although the app's own Sheet has all three (src/components/Sheet.tsx:19-36). In a DM, Block has no confirmation at all (src/app/chat/dm/[id]/page.tsx:24). Report silently files only the last message, with the reason 'Something else' and no reason picker (dm/[id]/page.tsx:25-26). The copy says 'THE CREW WILL LOOK AT IT' (PersonCard.tsx:55; dm/[id]/page.tsx:26) and 'Reports go to the Hoppaz crew' (PersonCard.tsx:103). But 'crew' is a user feature, and the community rules say 'Hoppaz staff review reports' (src/app/community/page.tsx:4).
findings.why: Safety tools that behave differently in two places, plus a browser pop-up, look unfinished. Giving destructive actions the same weight as Wave invites mis-taps. The draft's sheet motion is misregistration (a violet copy offset 6px for 120ms), not a generic slide-up.
findings.suggestion: Build the person sheet on the existing Sheet component. Make WAVE the only full-width orange lip button. Below it, put two small text actions: 'Block' in Fire Ant red and 'Report' in dim. Confirm Block inside the sheet ('Block Suya Rider 4F? You won't see each other.', with BLOCK / CANCEL) instead of a browser pop-up. In DMs, the flag and block icons open the same sheet with the same reason list. The reason is passed to the same report call that exists today. Change the copy to 'Reported. Hoppaz staff will review it.' Use the misregistration motion for this sheet.

findings.title: Cut the crew XP leaderboard
findings.evidence: src/app/crew/page.tsx:154-172 ranks you and your friends by XP, with a level name and XP on every row (line 168). Search results also show XP (crew/page.tsx:96). A separate Lagos monthly board already exists (src/app/quests/page.tsx:27). New users start at 'ROOKIE' (src/lib/brand.ts:32).
findings.why: The draft says 'two tiles, not eight': XP folds into one rank name, and the visible numbers are nights out and weekend streak. A friends-only XP table for a new crew is mostly '0 XP · ROOKIE' rows, which is depressing. It also competes with the shelf, which the draft calls 'a better retention mechanic than any score'.
findings.suggestion: Remove the leaderboard section and the XP figure in search results. If a crew needs any number, use one number tile under the crew name: a big Poppins Black '12' with a mono caption 'NIGHTS TOGETHER', counted from the stubs on the shelf.
findings.gamification_angle: A shared count ('nights together') builds a crew. A ranking inside a friend group splits it.

findings.title: Untangle 'crew' (groups) from 'crew' (friends list) and drop the fake distances
findings.evidence: The page title is 'Your crew' (src/app/crew/page.tsx:61) and the next section is 'YOUR CREWS' (line 66). The friends list below is a separate one-way list (src/lib/useCrew.ts:42-45, the `crew` table). The schema itself calls that table legacy, kept 'for the existing friend map and search experience' (supabase/schema.sql:1117-1118). Each friend row shows '~X km · ~Y min away' (crew/page.tsx:138), worked out from their home area (useCrew.ts:11; crew/page.tsx:128-130), not where they really are. Search results show any stranger's home area to anyone who types two letters of their name (crew/page.tsx:95-97).
findings.why: Two features with one name confuse people. A precise distance based on a home-area guess is false precision and reads like tracking. Showing strangers' home areas in search sits badly with the community rules' line on stalking (community/page.tsx:4).
findings.suggestion: Call the named groups 'Crews' and make them the page. Move the friends list behind a small 'People' link, or fold it into 'Add people to this crew'. On a friend's row, show only their area name ('Yaba'), with no km or minutes. In search results, show only name and face: no area, no XP.

findings.title: Simplify starting, joining and inviting; use the mascot on the empty state
findings.evidence: src/app/crew/page.tsx:66 shows an internal-sounding 'LONG-TERM GROUPS' tag. Line 67 squeezes the name input, a Private/Open dropdown and a + icon button onto one row. Line 68 always shows a 'Join with invite code' input. Line 70 lists up to 50 strangers' open crews (src/lib/game.ts:37 `.limit(50)`) inside your own crews box. The invite is a raw 10-character code (supabase/schema.sql:1124) in a tiny tag (crew/page.tsx:179). The empty copy for 'no friends' (crew/page.tsx:121-123) points to the map's crew button.
findings.why: Everything is open at once, so a first look at the tab is a form. Raw codes are hard to share. The draft wants things to be WhatsApp-shareable, and it lists empty states as an allowed mascot moment.
findings.suggestion: With zero crews, show a clean empty state: the mascot in its 'oya come' pose, one line ('Crews are the people you actually go out with'), and two buttons, START A CREW (orange lip) and JOIN WITH A CODE (ghost), each opening its own small sheet. Inside a crew, replace the code tag with an INVITE button. It opens the phone's share sheet with a ready message containing the code, which is a UI-only change. Move open crews behind a quiet 'Browse open crews' link. Remove the 'LONG-TERM GROUPS' tag.
findings.gamification_angle: A first-run moment with the mascot, plus a share-to-WhatsApp invite, is the growth loop for crews.

findings.title: One fallback for people who never dressed their Hopper
findings.evidence: Crew shows a letter in a square when there's no avatar (src/app/crew/page.tsx:187-197, `rounded`) and a round face otherwise (lines 199-205, `rounded-full`). Chat passes a missing look straight to Avatar (src/components/chat/ChatFace.tsx:24-25), which turns it into DEFAULT_LOOK (src/lib/avatar.ts:213-229, 245-266). So every undressed named person in a room shows the identical default face in the orange Hoppaz tee. The map uses a third style, a small cream letter dot (src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:759-765). The Me tab already has a 'Your look' nudge (src/app/me/page.tsx:141-148), but its copy says 'Your crew sees it on the map' (line 145).
findings.why: The same person looks three different ways depending on the tab, and a room full of identical default faces looks like a bug or a bot farm. Consistency is the cheapest professionalism win.
findings.suggestion: Use one rule everywhere. Dressed people show their head crop. Undressed people show their initial in Poppins Black on the same neutral round disc. Everything is round. Keep the existing 'Your look' card on Me, but change its line to something true, such as 'Dress your Hopper. It's how people see you in rooms and crews.' Never nudge on other people's faces.
findings.gamification_angle: Undressed people look visibly plain next to dressed ones, which gently pulls people toward the avatar editor without nagging.

findings.title: Hide real fashion-house names in the avatar wardrobe until they've agreed
findings.evidence: src/lib/avatar.ts:113-125 names 13 real Lagos and Nigerian labels (Orange Culture, Lagos Space Programme, Kenneth Ize, Tokyo James, Maki Oh and others). They sit next to the in-house Hoppaz merch (line 111) and the generic 'Yaba Okrika' market (line 112). The code's own note says 'Before this goes public, or before any of it is sold or sponsored, get each label's OK' (avatar.ts:107-109). The editor shows these names as filter chips (src/app/me/avatar/page.tsx:161-169) and as orange captions on every tile (line 315, used at 176 and 189). The Me card says 'Dress your Hopper in Lagos labels' (src/app/me/page.tsx:145).
findings.why: Showing real brands without permission looks unprofessional and risks legal and partner trouble at launch. Orange captions on tiles also break 'orange only for tap'.
findings.suggestion: Until a label signs, show items by description only ('Adire shirt', 'Aso-oke stripe shirt'). Group the filter chips by style (Streetwear, Native, Prints, Basics) instead of by brand. This is a display-only grouping, and the stored items don't change. Keep Hoppaz merch and Yaba Okrika named. Brand captions become dim mono, not orange. When a label signs, its name comes back with a 'COLLAB' tag.
findings.gamification_angle: Signed labels can return later as drop-only collab pieces, a natural use of violet for 'rare'.

findings.title: Replace 'WHO'S HERE' and per-person wave chips with a quiet face row
findings.evidence: src/app/chat/page.tsx:62 shows a 'WHO'S HERE' button that only re-fetches. The list already loads when the room opens (src/lib/chat.ts:144-146). The server returns nobody unless you have checked in at that event yourself (supabase/schema.sql:705-706). Most people tapping the button therefore see nothing happen, with no explanation. Line 64 renders one violet pill per person reading '<alias> · WAVE', and a tap waves straight away with no way to back out. The 'already waved' flag is returned (chat.ts:137; schema.sql:711) but never shown. The tab label 'WAVES & DMS' (chat/page.tsx:53) is jargon on first sight.
findings.why: A button that only refreshes, and often shows nothing, looks broken. One-tap waves from a strip of chips are easy to send by mistake. Violet is reserved for scarcity.
findings.suggestion: Remove the WHO'S HERE button. In an event room, show a small overlapping row of faces above the feed with a mono count ('7 HERE'). These are alias faces, because that's all the server shares. People you've already waved at get a small 'WAVED' mark. Tapping a face opens the existing person sheet, which already has Wave. If you haven't checked in, show one dim line instead: 'CHECK IN TO SEE WHO'S HERE'. Rename the second tab to 'Inbox' (the count is covered by the inbox finding).
findings.gamification_angle: Wave-back-to-unlock is the social game in Chat. Putting it behind a face makes it feel deliberate rather than spammy, and 'check in to see who's here' rewards actually showing up.

findings.title: Make the community rules readable and reachable from Chat
findings.evidence: src/app/community/page.tsx:4 sets the body of all five rules as `.hint` text, which is 11px dim mono (src/app/globals.css:66-68). The headings are already Poppins (`font-display text-lg font-black`). The back link is hard-coded to /me, although Privacy also links here (src/app/privacy/page.tsx:13). Chat only says 'Keep it friendly' (src/app/chat/page.tsx:66) and never links to the rules. The person sheet's report step doesn't either (src/components/chat/PersonCard.tsx:103).
findings.why: Long reading text should be Archivo at a comfortable size in cream, and mono is for labels and dates. At 11px dim mono, the rules look like small print nobody is meant to read, which undercuts the safety story.
findings.suggestion: Number the five rules 01–05 in mono. Keep the headings in Poppins and set the body in Archivo at 15px, in cream. Make the back arrow return to wherever you came from. Link 'community rules' from the empty-room line in Chat and from the report step in the person sheet.

questions_for_jae: Should the one-way friends list (the thing that drew faces on the map) survive at all once named Crews are the centre of the tab, or should 'people' just mean 'people in your crews'?

Check-ins and swipes are private to each person (supabase/schema.sql:430, 434). That means 'your crew is going' can only be shown on events your crew planned a move to, not for every event a friend likes. Is that OK for this UI pass?

The draft wants crew rooms that persist in Chat. Today any room is readable by anyone who knows its name (supabase/schema.sql:642-655 only checks event end and blocks), so a private crew room needs a back-end change. Is it OK to leave crew rooms out of this UI pass?
Do you want your own Hopper on the map at all, or a plain 'you are here' dot that only appears when GPS is on? (Recommendation: the plain dot.)

The draft allows the mascot on empty states but bans it on chat and on 'anything with a scroll'. Is the mascot OK on the zero-crews Crew screen? (Recommendation: yes there, and never inside Chat, including the empty Inbox.)
Have any of the fashion houses in the avatar wardrobe agreed to be named? If none have, can we show the clothes by description only for launch?
Anonymous posting in event rooms adds aliases, special faces and the mutual-reveal flow. Do you want to keep it for launch, or make Chat even plainer by dropping it?
Once XP leaves the screen, which single number (if any) should appear inside a crew: nights together, weekend streak, or nothing?
Should 'Plan a move' use the same 14-night rail as Tonight, with the month grid behind a calendar icon for plans further out?

verify:chrome-tokens.surface: App chrome, tokens, type and motion (globals.css, tailwind.config.ts, layout.tsx, BottomNav, Wordmark, TitleSequence, Toaster, Sheet, brand.ts, mapStyle.ts, manifest, icon, plus a sweep of src for raw hex, arbitrary values and emoji). Verified pass: every file:line below was opened and checked in the read-only copy.
verify:chrome-tokens.current_state_summary: Hoppaz runs one dark-only theme. Its small Tailwind palette (ink, ink-2, ink-3, orange, ember, cream, violet, dim, line, ok) is close to the draft's night set but not the same. There is no day theme, no Lagoon, Danfo or Fire Ant, and the green isn't Keke. Every word is set in Poppins, including body text at weight 400, with Space Mono for labels. Archivo and DM Mono, which the draft asks for, aren't installed. There is one orange button with an ember lip, but it has cream text that fails contrast, 4px corners and a 2px press. Other places already put dark text on orange, so the code isn't consistent with itself. Every container is a generic rounded card, so there is no ticket stub. Pills come in four styles and labels sit at 7-9px. On the map, a layer of extruded city buildings turns ember-orange as buildings get taller. It grows out of the ground with an overshoot, and tapping an event flies the camera straight into it at street zoom. Motion also breaks 'nothing moves': signs pop with an elastic bounce, the bus bobs forever, and the map swoops in for 3.4 seconds every time the Map tab opens. Toasts use violet as a general 'success' colour and cream for both errors and neutral notices, and a new badge arrives only as one of these 2.6-second toasts. Developer text and a STAFF link are visible to every player. The 11.7-second Lagos-skyline intro is well made and plays once. The 5-tab nav is calm, but its labels are 8px.

findings.title: Remove the orange 3D city buildings; keep 3D only at events
findings.evidence: src/lib/mapStyle.ts:104-135 addCityLayer() adds a 'hoppaz-city' fill-extrusion over every building in the basemap from zoom 13 (minzoom at line 118). Colour runs by height from BRAND.ink3 to #2E211C to BRAND.ember #B83600 (lines 121-126), and heights are exaggerated x2.2 (line 105), so tall blocks turn orange-brown. riseCity() at mapStyle.ts:141-151 grows them out of the ground with an overshoot curve (line 143). src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:179-189 adds the layer on load and fires the rise once zoom passes 13.4. Tapping an event eases the camera to zoom 15.6 at a 55-degree tilt (NightMap.tsx:685-695), which is exactly when this skyline surrounds the event. The only other 3D layer is the event 'lots' at NightMap.tsx:191-208: cream walls, an orange/ember roof and a crowd-colour diamond, built in src/lib/eventLots.ts:43-57. Lots are tappable (NightMap.tsx:351), so their orange roofs already follow 'orange = tap'. Two secondary sources of warm colour sit around events: the basemap's flat building shapes are tinted #3A2B23 (mapStyle.ts:41-47), and main roads and bridges are painted orange-tan #D88A4E / #C85E28 (mapStyle.ts:55-69). mapStyle.ts:16 states the intent as 'orange arteries'.
findings.why: Jae asked for exactly this. The draft says orange means 'you can tap this'. An ember skyline tells the eye the whole city is tappable and drowns out the event lots, the only 3D objects that mean anything.
findings.suggestion: Take the city-building layer and its grow-up animation off the map entirely. In code, that means stopping the addCityLayer and riseCity calls in NightMap.tsx:179-189. Keep the event lots, so the only 3D shapes left on the map are one little building per event. As a lighter follow-up, tone the flat building shapes and the orange-tan main roads down to warm greys close to the night ground. Then the only orange left on the map is the heat glow (which the draft's Map screen allows), the event signs and the event lots. The illustrated skyline can stay in the intro, because that's artwork and not map.
findings.gamification_angle: With nothing else standing up, each event's lot becomes a landmark worth zooming in on, and the map reads like a game board with pieces on it.

findings.title: Rebuild the colour tokens around the draft's four tiers
findings.evidence: tailwind.config.ts:11-19 and src/lib/brand.ts:2-12 define ink #0E0B0A; ink-2 #17110F (draft night raised is #171210); ink-3 #231915 (draft night card #221A17); line #2E211C (draft hairline #2E2320); dim #8A7C73 (draft #9C9087: 6.31:1 on the ground versus 4.87:1 today); ok #49D07A (draft Keke #2FD35C), used once at src/app/chat/page.tsx:61. Lagoon, Danfo and Fire Ant don't exist, so delete-account falls back to Tailwind's default red at src/app/me/page.tsx:271 (border-red-500 / text-red-400). Raw hex bypasses the tokens: lilac #A98CFF at src/app/globals.css:58, src/components/EventCard.tsx:140 and 154, src/app/me/page.tsx:285, src/app/page.tsx:227 and src/app/drops/page.tsx:18; a third violet #6F42D8 at globals.css:224; #a89588 at globals.css:86 and src/app/drop/page.tsx:109; own chat bubbles #4A2D1E/#2A1A12 at src/app/chat/page.tsx:71 and src/app/chat/dm/[id]/page.tsx:31; hard-coded dark map chrome at globals.css:79-97 and 263-275. Separate palettes: TitleSequence at src/components/TitleSequence.tsx:26-35, crowd tones at src/lib/crowd.ts:44-49, lot colours at src/lib/eventLots.ts:44-52, basemap hex at src/lib/mapStyle.ts:30-79. The header at tailwind.config.ts:4-5 ('black 60 / orange 25 / cream 10 / violet 5') contradicts the draft's rule that nothing orange is ever inert.
findings.why: The rest of the draft depends on these tokens existing under their real names: one state colour per card, day twins, and errors that look like errors. Today 'violet text' has three different hex values, and errors borrow Tailwind's default red.
findings.suggestion: Rename and re-value the palette to the draft's names. Grounds: ground, raised, card, hairline, text and dim, each with a night value and a day value. Action colours: orange and ember. State colours: keke, lagoon, danfo, violet and fireant, each with its darker day twin (#1FA847, #0E86B8, #B07F00, #4A20E0, #C62A2F). Replace every raw hex listed above with a token, so the intro, map signs, crowd colours and lots all draw from the same source. Delete the '25% orange' comment and write the rule 'orange only on things you can tap' in its place.
findings.gamification_angle: Named state colours (Keke for going, Violet for drops, Danfo for last tickets) become a visual language players learn, the way Duolingo's colours are.

findings.title: Add the day (cream) theme and switch it on the Lagos clock
findings.evidence: Only one theme exists. src/app/globals.css:7 sets 'color-scheme: dark' and globals.css:16 hard-sets the body to bg-ink/text-cream. src/app/layout.tsx:28 sets themeColor '#0E0B0A', and public/manifest.webmanifest:8-9 sets dark background and theme colours. The tokens are fixed hex in tailwind.config.ts:12-19, not CSS variables, so they can't swap. The map overrides at globals.css:79-97 and 263-275 are hard-coded dark. The basemap is always CARTO dark-matter (src/lib/mapStyle.ts:4-6), and the repaint at mapStyle.ts:19-89 is tuned only for dark. Lagos-time helpers already exist: clockLagos/dayLagos in src/lib/geo.ts:99-113 use 'Africa/Lagos'.
findings.why: The draft names this as one of the two decisions everything else hangs on: cream ground by day and black after dark, driven by the real time in Lagos, with each card carrying its own event's time. Its Map screen also asks for light tiles before sunset. Without this, daytime events (brunches, tech meetups) feel like they belong in a nightclub app.
findings.suggestion: Turn the colour tokens into two swappable sets, night and day, and switch the whole app between them on Lagos time. Each event card keeps the treatment of its own start time, so a brunch card stays cream inside the night app. The status-bar colour and map tiles follow the same switch. Engineering note: this is CSS variables plus a small client-side clock check using the existing Lagos helpers in geo.ts. No data changes.
findings.gamification_angle: The app visibly 'goes out' at sunset when the screen flips to night, which gives Hoppaz a daily moment without adding any animation.

findings.title: Swap fonts to Archivo (body) and DM Mono (labels); stop using thin Poppins
findings.evidence: src/app/layout.tsx:4-8 loads Poppins 400/600/900 and Space Mono 400/700. package.json:15-16 has only @fontsource/poppins and @fontsource/space-mono. src/app/globals.css:9 sets --font-mono to 'Space Mono', and globals.css:16 sets the body to font-display (Poppins), so all body text renders in Poppins 400. tailwind.config.ts:20-25 has only display and mono families. The src sweep finds 0 uses of font-medium or font-semibold; weights are 63x font-black and 63x font-bold. Most font-bold sits on mono labels. Where it sits on Poppins (src/components/SwipeDeck.tsx:232, src/components/EventQuestList.tsx:56, src/app/crew/page.tsx:70), it requests weight 700, which isn't loaded, so the browser substitutes a neighbouring weight.
findings.why: The draft sets Poppins Black for display, numbers and button labels, never below 600. Anything you read is Archivo 400/500/600, which is narrower and holds up at 13px on a dark ground. Labels, dates and prices are DM Mono. Space Mono is wider and quirkier, and reads less precise at the 8-11px sizes used everywhere.
findings.suggestion: Self-host Archivo and DM Mono the same way Poppins is loaded now. Make Archivo the default body font. Keep Poppins only for headlines, numbers and button labels, and drop Poppins 400. DM Mono comes without a bold, so mono labels lose their heavy look and use regular or medium weight. That's part of the 'precise' feel the draft wants. Keep the 'Noto Sans' fallback (tailwind.config.ts:22-24) so the naira sign still renders.

findings.title: Make the orange button a true lip button: dark label, 6px corners, 4px press
findings.evidence: src/app/globals.css:38-43: .btn is bg-orange text-cream, 'rounded' (4px), shadow-chunk (0 4px 0 #B83600, tailwind.config.ts:27), and on press moves only 2px (active:translate-y-0.5) onto a 2px lip (shadow-chunk-sm, tailwind.config.ts:28). Cream on #FF4D00 measures 2.82:1, below even the 3:1 large-text minimum; ink on orange is 5.9:1. The style is hand-copied at src/components/SwipeDeck.tsx:129 (round 'I'm in') and src/app/page.tsx:296-300 (map FAB). A selected map sign is cream on orange too (globals.css:232-236). Meanwhile the selected filter chips already use dark text on orange: src/components/FilterCard.tsx:95, src/app/discover/page.tsx:89, src/app/chat/page.tsx:58.
findings.why: The draft spec is a 4px hard ember edge with zero blur, 6px corners, and a press where the face drops exactly 4px so the lip disappears. Its mock shows dark labels on orange. Cream-on-orange is hard to read in Lagos sunlight on a cheap Android, and the code already disagrees with itself about label colour.
findings.suggestion: Use one button style everywhere: orange face, dark ink label in Poppins Black caps (about 14px), 6px corners, a solid ember lip underneath, and a press that sinks the full 4px so it feels like a real key. The round map FAB, the swipe 'I'm in' button and the selected map sign use the same colours instead of their own copies.
findings.gamification_angle: A press that physically bottoms out is the main tactile reward in the app. It's what makes 'I'm going' and 'Claim drop' feel like pressing a game button.

findings.title: Hide developer and staff UI from players
findings.evidence: Every player sees a STAFF link to /admin on Me (src/app/me/page.tsx:269). The client already loads the is_admin flag: profiles are fetched with select('*') at src/lib/useSession.ts:20, and Profile.is_admin is typed at src/lib/types.ts:36. When offline, Me shows developer instructions to players: 'Add the Supabase keys and turn on anonymous sign-ins' (me/page.tsx:284-288). The map shows 'DEMO NIGHT · NOT CONNECTED TO THE DATABASE' or 'LIVE EVENT DATA UNAVAILABLE · CHECK DATABASE SETUP' whenever demo is true (src/app/page.tsx:226-230). demo starts as true with demo events pre-filled (src/lib/useEvents.ts:20-21), so the banner can flash on a cold open in production until the first fetch returns. It is also set back to true in production if that fetch fails (useEvents.ts:44-48). A second banner reads 'PRODUCTION DATABASE NOT CONFIGURED' (page.tsx:231-235).
findings.why: Jae asked to remove unnecessary UI. Database setup hints and staff links are for the team, not players, and they make the product look unfinished at the exact moment it's being judged.
findings.suggestion: Show the STAFF link only to staff, using the is_admin flag the app already loads. Staff can also just bookmark /admin. Keep the database banners in development builds only. For players, a failed load becomes a proper error state: a plain line ('Can't reach tonight's map. Pull to try again.'), with the mascot in its 'oops' pose, since the draft allows the mascot on errors. Rewrite the offline note on Me as a player line: 'You're offline. Your nights will save when you're back.'
findings.gamification_angle: Errors handled by the mascot feel like part of the game rather than a broken app.

findings.title: Cut ambient and bouncy motion; use one 'stamp' and the sheet 'misregistration'
findings.evidence: tailwind.config.ts:31-40 defines pop (fade and 8px slide), pulse2 (infinite loop) and rise (sheet slide, 260ms). pulse2 is used only by the intro's star twinkle (globals.css:137-139). Map signs pop with an elastic overshoot, cubic-bezier(0.34,1.8,...) at src/app/globals.css:208-212, staggered per sign at src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:592. The Hop bus bobs forever while moving (globals.css:277-292, toggled at NightMap.tsx:733). The city buildings spring up with an overshoot (src/lib/mapStyle.ts:137-151). The map swoops from a zoomed-out view into a tilted city over 3.4 seconds (NightMap.tsx:779-797). The map is created on mount and destroyed on unmount (NightMap.tsx:127-150, 380), so the swoop, sign pops and city rise replay every time you return to the Map tab. Toasts slide in (src/components/Toaster.tsx:14). The avatar re-pops on every change (src/app/me/avatar/page.tsx:75). Sheets slide up with animate-rise at src/components/Sheet.tsx:38, src/components/EventCard.tsx:84, src/components/FilterCard.tsx:40 and src/components/chat/PersonCard.tsx:64. Reduced motion is honoured for CSS at globals.css:294-302, but the JS-driven city rise and camera swoop ignore it.
findings.why: The draft: stamp, not bounce (180ms, hard ease-out, no elastic overshoot). Sheets rise with a violet copy offset six pixels for 120ms, then snap into place. On the map, scrubbing the time slider is the only ambient motion, and everywhere else nothing moves. Holding back is what gives the drop reveal its punch.
findings.suggestion: Replace pop, pulse2 and every overshoot curve with one 'stamp' animation: a quick scale-down onto the surface, a degree or two off-square, 180ms. Use it only for badges, rank changes and 'I'm going'. Sheets keep their quick rise, but add the draft's violet ghost copy six pixels off for 120ms before it snaps into place. Map signs simply appear, and the bus slides between stops without bobbing. Play the map swoop once per app open (or only on first run), not on every tab switch, and skip it for people with reduced motion on.
findings.gamification_angle: If everything bounces, nothing feels like a reward. Saving the stamp and star flight for real achievements makes them feel earned.

findings.title: Turn badge unlocks and rank-ups into a real moment, not a toast
findings.evidence: When a check-in earns a badge, the only feedback is a toast: say('BADGE UNLOCKED · ...', 'violet') at src/lib/useCheckin.ts:66-69. It vanishes after 2.6 seconds (src/lib/store.ts:73) and looks like any other notice (src/components/Toaster.tsx:13-18). No stamp or star-flight component exists. The only stamp keyframe is the intro wordmark's (src/app/globals.css:192-201, used at src/components/TitleSequence.tsx:367). The Me tab has no target for an incoming reward (src/components/BottomNav.tsx:13). The badge key is already returned with the check-in (useCheckin.ts:66).
findings.why: The draft names a badge or rank change as one of the few 'moments'. It gets the loud layer, a 180ms stamp, a star flight into the Me tab, and the mascot (celebrate/win). Right now the biggest reward in the game looks the same as 'QR CODE READ'.
findings.suggestion: When a badge arrives, show a short full-width card over the current screen. The badge, drawn as a stub, stamps onto it slightly off-square, the mascot plays its celebrate pose, and a small star then flies to the Me tab, which pops once. Tap anywhere to dismiss. Plain check-ins ('Checked in · +50 XP') stay a quiet toast, because the draft says never to animate each individual point. No new data is needed: the badge key already comes back from the check-in.
findings.gamification_angle: This is the payoff that makes people go to one more event. A stamp-and-fly sequence that only happens a few times a month is what they'll screenshot.

findings.title: Show one rank name, not two ladders that share names
findings.evidence: There are two rank systems with overlapping names. The XP ladder in src/lib/brand.ts:30-37 runs ROOKIE, HOPPER, NIGHT RUNNER, BRIDGE RAT, CAPTAIN. The Hops ladder on Me (src/app/me/page.tsx:75, 162-166) shows HOPPER or CAPTAIN based on bus rides. The map HUD shows the XP rank, XP number and an orange progress bar (src/app/page.tsx:146-162). The Me header shows XP rank and XP (me/page.tsx:93), and the card just below shows the Hops rank (me/page.tsx:162). Crew lists show the XP rank (src/app/crew/page.tsx:168). A player with 1,400 XP and no bus rides reads 'CAPTAIN' in the header and 'HOPPER' in the card on the same screen.
findings.why: The draft's Me screen has one rank name in large Poppins Black, with everything else derived into it, plus two number tiles. Two contradictory ranks on one screen read as a bug, not a game.
findings.suggestion: Pick one ladder to show by name everywhere (map, Me, Crew) and hide the other from view until Jae decides how they merge. Take the XP chip off the map HUD: the draft's Map screen has no HUD stats. Show the rank big on Me, where the draft puts it. This only hides and moves existing labels; no scoring changes.
findings.gamification_angle: One rank name that stamps when it changes is a clear status players chase and flex. Two names cancel each other out.

findings.title: Create the ticket stub as the one event container
findings.evidence: The only container is .card at src/app/globals.css:47-49 (bg-ink-2, 1px line border, rounded-md, no notches). Corners drift: rounded-lg (8px) at src/components/EventCard.tsx:84, src/components/FilterCard.tsx:40, src/components/SwipeDeck.tsx:155 and src/components/chat/PersonCard.tsx:64; rounded-t-lg at src/components/Sheet.tsx:37; rounded-xl at src/app/report/share/[token]/page.tsx:10. The radius tally across src: 49 rounded, 23 rounded-full, 8 rounded-sm, 6 rounded-md, 4 rounded-lg, 1 rounded-xl, 1 rounded-t-lg, 1 rounded-t-sm.
findings.why: The draft calls the stub the signature container and the reason Hoppaz won't look like every other dark event app. Anything that stands for one night is a stub with two punched notches: an event in a list, a badge, a claimed drop, a deck card. It should be recognisable at thumbnail size and in a WhatsApp share.
findings.suggestion: Build one 'stub' piece: card colour, hairline border, 6px corners, and two half-circle notches punched out of the left and right edges. Inside: the title in Poppins Black caps, then one DM Mono line (day · area · price), then at most one coloured pill. Make day and night versions, and use it in Tonight, the swipe deck, Crew's shelf, the badge shelf and claimed drops. Square every other corner to 6px.
findings.gamification_angle: Stubs are collectibles. A shelf of punched stubs is the draft's retention mechanic ('a shared memory rather than a number').

findings.title: Merge four pill styles into one status pill and one filter chip
findings.evidence: .tag at src/app/globals.css:50-59 is mono 8.5px with a grey border, dim text and 2px corners; .tag-v uses the off-token #A98CFF. Filter chips at src/components/FilterCard.tsx:94 are rounded-full Poppins Black 11px. Date chips at src/app/discover/page.tsx:87 are rounded-full mono 9px. Channel chips at src/app/chat/page.tsx:58 are rounded-full mono 9.5px. The status-tag style is also used as tappable buttons: the I'M IN / MAYBE / CAN'T GO buttons at src/app/crew/page.tsx:181 and the WAVE buttons at src/app/chat/page.tsx:64.
findings.why: The draft has exactly one pill: mono caps, a 1px border in a state colour, a transparent fill. It's the only place a state colour appears on a card. Today status labels and tappable buttons share one look, so players can't tell what's tappable.
findings.suggestion: Make two pieces. First, a status pill that isn't tappable: DM Mono caps at about 10-11px, a thin border in the one state colour, a see-through fill (green '14 GOING', violet 'DROP AT 11', yellow '6 SPOTS', blue 'DAYTIME'). Second, a filter chip that is tappable: same shape, turning solid orange with dark text when selected, which matches how the draft's night rail marks the chosen day. RSVP and wave actions become small lip buttons or filter chips, never status pills.
findings.gamification_angle: Players learn the colour code fast (green = friends going, violet = drop, yellow = nearly gone), and the pills become scarcity cues that drive FOMO.

findings.title: Stop painting surfaces with state colours and stop putting orange on things you can't tap
findings.evidence: Violet fills: the whole toast (src/components/Toaster.tsx:17), the Captain number tile (src/app/me/page.tsx:169), Hop stop numbers (src/components/HopSheet.tsx:43), the bus label (src/components/map/NightMap.tsx:722) and anonymous chat faces (src/components/chat/ChatFace.tsx:28). Violet-tinted panels: src/components/EventCard.tsx:139 and 152, src/app/me/page.tsx:230, src/app/collection/page.tsx:19, src/app/drops/page.tsx:18.
