Orange on things that aren't tappable: the Sheet's top border (src/components/Sheet.tsx:38); the orange disc behind the avatar on the Me card (me/page.tsx:152); the orange-tinted Outside Score panel (me/page.tsx:220); orange squares beside each past night (me/page.tsx:244); orange progress bars and level name (src/app/page.tsx:151 and 158, me/page.tsx:174); orange author names in the event card's chat preview (EventCard.tsx:246); the price in orange (EventCard.tsx:98 and 270); the HEAT label and gradient on swipe-deck cards (src/components/HeatBar.tsx:4-7, used at src/components/SwipeDeck.tsx:180); the 'How the night goes' chart bars (EventCard.tsx:169-190, which Jae already wants cut). The Wordmark carries the exact button lip (src/components/Wordmark.tsx:9) but isn't a link (src/app/page.tsx:143-145).
findings.why: In the draft, Tier 2 never paints a surface ('the moment a card has a green background the system is broken'), and nothing orange is ever inert. The draft does allow orange heat on the map itself, but not as decoration on cards. The Wordmark is the worst case: it looks exactly like a button and does nothing.
findings.suggestion: Keep solid fills for the grounds and for orange buttons. Violet, green and the other state colours appear only as text, a thin border, a dot or an icon. Replace the Sheet's orange top edge with the hairline. Make progress bars and past-night markers cream or dim, show the price in DM Mono cream, and drop the orange tint from the Outside Score panel. On deck cards, swap the heat bar for the stub's 'N going' pill. The orange sun behind the rider in the avatar editor is artwork and can stay (src/app/me/avatar/page.tsx:73-74); the disc on the Me card goes. Remove the lip from the logo so it stops looking like a button.
findings.gamification_angle: When orange always means 'do something', the one orange thing on each screen becomes the obvious next move.

findings.title: Make toasts read as done, failed or drop
findings.evidence: src/components/Toaster.tsx:13-18: the default tone is named 'orange' but renders cream-on-ink; the 'violet' tone fills the whole toast violet. It uses an arbitrary shadow, Poppins Black 12px and animate-pop. src/lib/store.ts:64-74 allows only two tones and hides after 2.6s. In practice violet is used as a generic success colour: 'CREW CREATED', 'JOINED THE CREW' (src/app/crew/page.tsx:67-70), 'QR CODE READ' (src/components/EventCard.tsx:147), 'QUEST SAVED' and 'PARTNER ADDED' (src/app/admin/page.tsx:19-20), 'MONTHLY REPORT LINK COPIED' (src/app/quests/page.tsx:26). Errors use the default cream tone, the same as many successes. Check-in failures (src/lib/useCheckin.ts:56-61) and 'CHECKED IN · +XP' (useCheckin.ts:71) look identical. A photo upload shows its error or 'PHOTO POSTED' in one tone (EventCard.tsx:216). Other errors on cream: src/app/chat/page.tsx:42, EventCard.tsx:144, src/app/drop/page.tsx:95, src/app/me/page.tsx:271.
findings.why: Tier 2 never paints a surface, Fire Ant red is for errors only, and violet means scarcity. A failed action that looks like a success is a trust problem as much as a looks problem.
findings.suggestion: Use one plain toast: a card-coloured box with a hairline border and a small coloured dot in front (green for done, red for failed, violet only for drops and rewards). Write the text as a short plain line instead of shouting caps, and stamp it in instead of sliding it. Engineering note: the tone parameter already exists (store.ts:65-66). Add an 'error' option, pass it at the error call sites above, and move admin and crew confirmations off violet.
findings.gamification_angle: Keep violet toasts rare, for drops only, so seeing one means something special happened.

findings.title: Bottom nav: bigger labels and your own face on the Me tab
findings.evidence: src/components/BottomNav.tsx:8-14 has 5 tabs: MAP (Map), TONIGHT (Flame), CREW (Users), CHAT (MessageSquare), ME (Star). Labels are font-mono text-[8px] at line 41, and icons are 17px at line 40. The active tab turns orange (line 37). Me stays highlighted on /quests, /drops and /collection (line 28). Nothing bounces; there's only transition-colors at line 36. A head crop of the avatar already exists and is used on Me (src/app/me/page.tsx:86, crop='head'), and the local look is stored at src/lib/store.ts:19.
findings.why: 8px mono labels are below comfortable phone legibility. The draft's star flight sends earned things into the Me tab, which 'pops', so that tab needs a clear, personal target. On the active colour: the draft's night rail shows the selected day as solid orange, so orange-for-selected is consistent with the draft.
findings.suggestion: Keep the five tabs and the calm behaviour. Raise labels to about 10px DM Mono. Keep the current tab in orange, matching how the draft marks the chosen night on the rail. Replace the star on Me with a tiny head crop of the player's own avatar, which is already stored on the phone, so no new data is needed. This is the player's face, not the mascot. The Me tab's only motion is a single pop when a reward lands.
findings.gamification_angle: Your own face in the nav is where badges, rank-ups and drops fly to, so every reward lands somewhere personal.

findings.title: Keep the opening title sequence, but cut it to about 5 seconds and let a tap skip it
findings.evidence: src/components/TitleSequence.tsx:22-24: START 0.5s + PAN 9s + 2.2s = 11.7s. The same timings are duplicated in CSS (src/app/globals.css:103-109), so both places must change together. There is elastic overshoot on buildings and signs (globals.css:110-125: ts-rise 1.56, ts-pop 1.8) and on the wordmark stamp (TitleSequence.tsx:367, bezier .34,1.7), plus an infinite star twinkle (globals.css:137-139). Skipping works only via the small top-right SKIP (TitleSequence.tsx:382-387) or Esc/Enter/Space (lines 118-120). The full-screen root at lines 242-243 has no tap handler. It plays once (seenTitle in src/lib/store.ts:16-17, 40), can be replayed from Me (src/app/me/page.tsx:274-282), and holds back the location prompt until it ends (src/app/page.tsx:93-103). No mascot appears.
findings.why: The draft allows the loud layer and the mascot on first run, so the intro belongs. But 11.7 seconds before a first-timer even sees the map, followed by a permission prompt, is long, and the elastic bounce goes against 'stamp, not bounce'. Its 'buildings grow out of the ground' idea is also what spread onto the real map as the orange city (src/lib/mapStyle.ts:97-99, 137-139).
findings.suggestion: Keep it as first-run artwork; it's a strong, very Lagos piece. Shorten the camera pan to about 4-5 seconds, let a tap anywhere skip it, and swap the bouncy pops for quick stamps. End on the wordmark with the mascot in its 'welcome' pose, since first run is one of the places the mascot is allowed. Keep the replay option in Me.
findings.gamification_angle: A short, skippable intro feels like a game boot screen rather than an ad, and ending on the mascot introduces the character who later shows up at drops and rank-ups.

findings.title: Replace emoji used as icons with drawn badge art and line icons
findings.evidence: Badge icons are emoji (bridge, palm tree, moon, ticket, microphone, beach umbrella, pushpin, bus) at src/lib/brand.ts:53-61, rendered on Me at src/app/me/page.tsx:192-217. Quest icons are emoji (camera, people, light bulb, pin) at src/app/quests/page.tsx:43 and src/components/EventQuestList.tsx:52. There's a gift emoji on the drop panel (src/components/EventCard.tsx:142) and a sparkles emoji on Me (src/app/me/page.tsx:231). Tick characters sit inside button labels at EventCard.tsx:114 and 162. Collectibles render an emoji that comes from data (collectible.emoji at EventCard.tsx:159 and src/app/collection/page.tsx:19). The admin API stores a sparkles emoji as the default badge icon (src/app/api/admin/game/route.ts:58). That one is back end, so leave it.
findings.why: Emoji look different on every phone (Samsung, Apple, older Android) and read as unfinished next to precise Poppins and DM Mono chrome. The draft makes badges into stubs and keeps illustration inside artwork.
findings.suggestion: Draw small stamp-style illustrations for the eight built-in badges, shown on a stub and identical on every phone. Quest types and the drop panel use the line-icon set the nav already uses. Use a drawn check icon instead of the tick character in buttons. Collectible emoji come from admin data, so keep showing them for now, but inside one fixed-size stub frame so they at least sit consistently.
findings.gamification_angle: Custom badge art is collectible and screenshot-worthy. A shelf of real stamps motivates far more than a row of emoji.

findings.title: Set a real type scale: bigger mono labels, stats as big display numbers
findings.evidence: There are ten arbitrary font sizes across src: text-[8px] x10, [8.5px] x2, [9px] x38, [9.5px] x1, [10px] x24, [11px] x14, [12px] x1, [12.5px] x1, [13px] x3, [13.5px] x2. The map's collectible label is 7px (src/app/globals.css:226). There are six arbitrary letter-spacings (0.08em-0.2em). The shared label classes are 8.5-9px: globals.css:51 (.tag), 61 (.label), 64 (.seclabel). Numbers render as small text: the Captain count is text-xs in a small violet chip (src/app/me/page.tsx:169-171), XP is mono 10px (src/app/page.tsx:154), and Outside Score is text-2xl/24px (me/page.tsx:222), below the draft's 32px. tabular-nums appears only 6 times.
findings.why: The draft says numbers are display type: stats at 32px and up in Poppins Black, tabular, with a mono caption underneath, and never set as body text. Mono at 7-9px on a dark ground doesn't hold up on a cheap Android screen.
findings.suggestion: Define a short set of sizes and use only those. Archivo: body 14px and small body 13px. DM Mono: labels 10px and pills 11px. Poppins Black display: 20, 28 and 40px. Any number a player cares about (nights out, streak, hops to Captain) shows big and bold with a small mono caption underneath, like the draft's two number tiles. Nothing on the map goes below 10px.
findings.gamification_angle: Big, bold numbers are the most transferable Duolingo trick. A large '7 NIGHTS OUT' is something people screenshot and try to beat.

findings.title: Make the home-screen icon and install metadata work on every phone
findings.evidence: public/manifest.webmanifest:10-12 lists one SVG icon marked 'any maskable'. public/icon.svg:8-15 draws the letters as live text in 'Poppins, Arial Black', but the OS draws the icon where Poppins isn't loaded, so the letters fall back to another font. The H and A sit near the corners (icon.svg:9, 13), outside the safe zone that Android's round masks keep. There's no PNG and no apple-touch-icon, and iOS doesn't reliably use SVG manifest icons. Theme and background colours are fixed dark (manifest.webmanifest:8-9, src/app/layout.tsx:28). Separately, src/app/layout.tsx:26 sets maximumScale: 1, which blocks pinch-zoom on Android. Its original reason, iOS zooming into focused inputs, is already handled by the 16px input size at src/app/globals.css:30.
findings.why: The draft's install sheet ('Share then Add to Home Screen' on iOS) only pays off if what lands on the home screen looks like Hoppaz.
findings.suggestion: Export the icon as fixed PNG artwork (180, 192 and 512px, plus a padded maskable version), with the letters turned into shapes so they always look right. Point the manifest and the iPhone icon tag at those files. Remove the zoom lock so people can pinch-zoom text pages; the map handles its own gestures.
findings.gamification_angle: A correct, bold icon on the home screen is the reward at the end of the install moment the draft designs for.

Lip button label colour: the code puts cream on orange (2.82:1, which fails contrast), but the filter chips already put dark text on orange, and the draft's mock reads as dark. Can we confirm dark ink labels on all orange buttons?

Day/night switch: should it flip at fixed Lagos times (for example 6:30pm and 6:30am) or follow actual sunset? And should the map tiles follow the same switch, with light tiles by day as the draft's Map screen says?
Title sequence: keep the Lagos-skyline intro as the first-run moment, cut to about 5 seconds and ending on the mascot's 'welcome' pose? Or replace it with a mascot-led first run?
Map swoop: today the map flies in from a zoomed-out view for 3.4 seconds every time you open the Map tab. Should it play once per app open, only on the very first run, or never?

Active tab colour: the draft's night rail marks the selected day in solid orange, so I've recommended keeping the active tab orange to match. Or would you rather use cream there, keeping orange strictly for 'tap to act'?

Rank: which ladder is the real one? The XP ladder (Rookie, Hopper, Night Runner, Bridge Rat, Captain) or the bus-ride ladder (Hopper to Captain)? And which two numbers go on Me: nights out + weekend streak (the draft's recommendation) or Outside Score? This decides whether the XP chip on the map goes.
Map roads: OK to tone the orange-tan main roads and bridges down to warm greys, so the only orange on the map is heat, event signs and event lots?
Badges: commission eight small stamp illustrations now, or ship plain line icons first and swap in art later?
Should the logo on the map be removed altogether to give the map more room? The draft's Map screen doesn't call for a logo, and today it looks like a button but does nothing.
